title: Tungsten Alloy Screws for Vacuum Sintering Furnaces
text: Vacuum sintering technology is widely used in the manufacturing fields of cemented carbides, advanced ceramics, powder metallurgy, new energy materials, and refractory metal products. With continuously increasing sintering temperatures and increasingly complex process conditions, key components inside furnaces are exposed to more severe working environments. As important connecting elements in hot-zone structures, fasteners must not only maintain reliable mechanical connections but also ensure high-temperature stability, vacuum cleanliness, and long-term cyclic service performance. CTIA GROUP and its parent company, CHINATUNGSTEN ONLINE, have been dedicated to the tungsten-molybdenum products industry for nearly 30 years. They specialize in providing flexible, customized global services for tungsten-molybdenum products, designing, manufacturing, and precisely processing various standard specifications, grades, and dimensional precision according to customer requirements, suitable for a wide range of applications. For more information on tungsten alloy, please visit the website : http://www.tungsten-alloy.com/index.htm . If you require tungsten alloy, please contact CTIA GROUP: sales@chinatungsten.com, 0592-5129595 . Among many high-temperature materials, tungsten alloy has gradually become an important material choice for fasteners in the hot zone of vacuum sintering furnaces due to its high melting point, high density, low thermal expansion coefficient, and good vacuum adaptability. Tungsten alloy screws produced by CTIA GROUP have been widely used in graphite fixtures, thermal insulation systems, temperature measurement components, and high-temperature support structures. 1.Technical Requirements for Fasteners under Vacuum Sintering Furnace Conditions Depending on the process, the operating temperature of vacuum sintering furnaces typically ranges from 1200°C to 2400°C. Some advanced equipment must also maintain a high vacuum state for long periods and operate with protective atmospheres such as argon, nitrogen, and hydrogen. Under such conditions, conventional fasteners are prone to issues such as high-temperature softening leading to reduced preload force, thread clearance changes caused by thermal cycling, metal volatilization contaminating sintered products, atmospheric corrosion causing surface damage, and creep deformation after long-term use. Therefore, hot-zone connectors inside the furnace must have higher material stability and environmental adaptability. The interior of vacuum furnaces widely uses graphite, tungsten plates, molybdenum plates, and silicon carbide components, all of which generally have low thermal expansion coefficients. If the expansion of fasteners is too large, additional stress may be generated during heating and cooling cycles, leading to loosening of connections or structural deformation. Therefore, it is particularly important to select fasteners with thermal expansion properties close to those of hot-zone materials. 2.Tungsten Alloy Screws for Vacuum Sintering Furnaces Tungsten-nickel-copper alloys produced by CTIA GROUP combine high density and good machinability, and are a commonly used tungsten alloy type in medium-temperature and high-vacuum equipment. The characteristics of tungsten-nickel-copper alloys include high density, non-magnetic properties, low thermal expansion coefficient, and low volatilization in vacuum environments, making them suitable for vacuum furnace systems. Compared with tungsten-nickel-copper alloys, tungsten-nickel-iron alloys generally have higher strength and toughness. Their characteristics include higher tensile strength, better impact resistance, stronger high-temperature load-bearing capacity, and greater suitability for large fixtures and heavy-load connection structures. In long-term high-temperature sintering equipment operation, tungsten-nickel-iron alloys are often used in connection parts with higher load-bearing requirements. 3.Applications of Tungsten Alloy Screws in Vacuum Sintering Furnaces Graphite fixture fixing systems: graphite trays, boats, and sintering fixtures are the most common hot-zone components inside furnaces. Tungsten alloy screws can achieve good thermal expansion matching with graphite materials, maintaining connection stability during repeated heating and cooling cycles, and reducing the impact of fixture displacement on product quality. Insulation shield and reflective shield connections: ultra-high-temperature vacuum furnaces usually adopt multilayer tungsten or molybdenum plates to form thermal reflection structures. Using tungsten alloy screws for fastening in these areas can reduce thermal deformation differences between different materials, improve the overall stability of insulation components, and reduce maintenance frequency during long-term operation. Temperature measurement component installation: high-temperature vacuum furnaces widely use thermocouples or infrared temperature measurement systems to monitor temperature changes. Tungsten alloy fasteners, due to their low vapor pressure and good thermal stability, can be used to secure thermocouple brackets and related measuring accessories, reducing the impact of impurity release on measurement accuracy in high-temperature environments. Furnace door and inner lining structure connections: the interior of some annealing and sintering furnaces adopts multilayer insulation structures in furnace doors. Tungsten alloy screws can maintain high dimensional stability during long-term thermal cycling, helping to maintain the reliability of sealing structures and reduce the risk of vacuum leakage.

title: Tungsten Alloy Screws for Medical Equipment
text: With the development of medical equipment toward higher precision, miniaturization, and greater reliability, the selection of materials for key structural components has received increasing attention. Tungsten alloy, as an engineering material that combines high density, high strength, and excellent shielding performance, has attracted extensive attention in recent years in the fields of medical imaging equipment, radiotherapy systems, and precision surgical instruments. Among them, tungsten alloy screws produced by CTIA GROUP, as important fastening components, not only perform structural connection functions but also meet requirements for radiation protection, weight balancing, and adaptability to special environments, providing new material solutions for modern medical device design. CTIA GROUP and its parent company, CHINATUNGSTEN ONLINE, have been dedicated to the tungsten-molybdenum products industry for nearly 30 years. They specialize in providing flexible, customized global services for tungsten-molybdenum products, designing, manufacturing, and precisely processing various standard specifications, grades, and dimensional precision according to customer requirements, suitable for a wide range of applications. For more information on tungsten alloy, please visit the website : http://www.tungsten-alloy.com/index.htm . If you require tungsten alloy, please contact CTIA GROUP: sales@chinatungsten.com, 0592-5129595 . 1.Characteristics of Tungsten Alloy Screws for Medical Equipment The density of tungsten alloys can typically reach 16.5–18.8 g/cm³, which is much higher than that of ordinary stainless steel and most engineering alloys. The high-density characteristic enables tungsten alloys to achieve greater mass concentration within limited space, offering significant advantages in the design of internal counterweight systems in medical equipment. Meanwhile, high density gives tungsten alloys excellent X-ray and gamma-ray absorption capability, making them an important material for medical radiation shielding components. Medical equipment operates in continuous working conditions for long periods, which imposes high requirements on the strength and stability of fasteners. Tungsten alloy has relatively high tensile strength and hardness, with tensile strength generally reaching above 700 MPa, and some high-performance materials can be further improved after heat treatment. This excellent mechanical performance enables tungsten alloy screws to withstand vibration loads, impact loads, and long-term fatigue stress under complex working conditions, thereby ensuring structural reliability during equipment operation. Hospital environments commonly involve disinfectants such as alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, and hypochlorite. Tungsten alloy exhibits good chemical stability in conventional medical environments and can effectively resist the corrosive effects of various disinfectants and cleaning agents, maintaining dimensional accuracy and surface quality during long-term use. In addition, tungsten alloy screws produced by CTIA GROUP are non-toxic and non-radioactive, and do not cause significant harm to humans or the environment. Some non-magnetic tungsten alloy screws (tungsten-nickel-copper alloy screws) can also be applied in components related to magnetic resonance imaging equipment, helping to reduce material interference with magnetic field environments. 2.Main Application Areas in Medical Equipment In medical linear accelerators, gamma knife systems, and radiotherapy auxiliary systems, tungsten alloys are widely used in the manufacture of collimators, shielding modules, and related fixed structures. Tungsten alloy screws can maintain stable mechanical performance in high-radiation environments, thereby further improving the positioning accuracy of key components. Due to their inherent radiation absorption capability, they can also contribute to enhancing overall shielding performance in certain structural designs. CT scanning systems, PET (Positron Emission Tomography), and nuclear medicine equipment typically require high-precision beam control devices. Tungsten alloy screws can be used to secure collimation structures and shielding modules, helping to maintain the accuracy of beam paths, improve image quality, and reduce radiation exposure in non-target areas. Large medical equipment often involves high-speed rotating mechanisms, such as CT gantries and radiotherapy rotational treatment systems. Due to the high density per unit volume of tungsten alloys, they can provide the required counterweight within limited installation space, enabling equipment center-of-gravity optimization and balance control, thereby reducing vibration and improving operational precision. 3.Standard Testing System for Medical Tungsten Alloy Screws Before leaving the factory, medical tungsten alloy screws produced by CTIA GROUP are usually required to undergo multiple performance verification tests, including chemical composition analysis, tensile strength testing, hardness testing, dimensional accuracy inspection, metallographic structure analysis, corrosion resistance testing, and biocompatibility evaluation.

title: How Is the Strength of Tungsten Alloy Screws?
text: The tungsten alloy screws produced by CTIA GROUP are mainly manufactured using a powder metallurgy process, consisting of tungsten as the hard phase and nickel-iron or nickel-copper as the binder phase. Alloys of different specifications differ in tungsten content, binder phase type, and thermal processing techniques, which result in differences in their mechanical properties. The strength characteristics of tungsten alloy screws are reflected in high density, high hardness, and certain toughness, making them suitable for applications requiring high loads and counterweighting. CTIA GROUP and its parent company, CHINATUNGSTEN ONLINE, have been dedicated to the tungsten-molybdenum products industry for nearly 30 years. If you require tungsten alloy, please contact CTIA GROUP: sales@chinatungsten.com, 0592-5129595 . I. Strength of Tungsten Alloy Screws According to industry standards, the ultimate tensile strength of tungsten alloy screws has specified minimum values, depending on the grade and binder phase type. Typical data are as follows: when using a nickel-iron binder phase, the minimum ultimate tensile strength ranges from 648 MPa to 758 MPa. When using a nickel-copper binder phase, the minimum ultimate tensile strength is 648 MPa. The 0.2% yield strength is generally in the range of 517 MPa to 550 MPa. The elongation is typically between 2% and 5%. The hardness range is mostly 32 HRC to 35 HRC. Under certain specific thermomechanical processing techniques, the ultimate tensile strength of tungsten alloy screws can be further increased to 900 MPa to 1200 MPa, with the yield strength increasing correspondingly, but the elongation will decrease accordingly. These parameters indicate that tungsten alloy screws have a relatively high strength level at room temperature, especially suitable for application environments that withstand static or medium-to-high frequency dynamic loads. Under high-temperature conditions, the strength remains stable, but attention should be paid to possible softening of the binder phase. II. Factors Affecting the Strength of Tungsten Alloy Screws The strength of tungsten alloy screws is closely related to sintering process parameters. Adequate sintering temperature and holding time help improve density and interfacial bonding strength, thereby enhancing overall tensile performance. The type of binder phase is also an important factor; the nickel-iron binder phase generally has higher strength and toughness than the nickel-copper binder phase at the same tungsten content. Grain size control, thermal processing (such as extrusion or forging), and residual stress elimination also significantly affect performance. After thermal processing, both material strength and hardness are improved, but plastic deformation capability decreases accordingly. In the geometric design of the screw structure, the thread portion and the screw diameter are areas of strength concentration. Diameters that are too large or too small affect engagement strength and load-bearing capacity. Improper torque control during installation may cause local stress to exceed the material's allowable range, thus affecting service life. III. Performance of Tungsten Alloy Screw Strength in Different Application Environments Tungsten alloy screws exhibit excellent tensile and yield strength at room temperature or ambient conditions, suitable for precision connection and counterweight requirements. In higher temperature environments, their strength remains good, making them suitable for high-temperature operation applications. Compared to other materials, tungsten alloy screws show stable performance in applications requiring high density, but under cyclic temperature changes or impact load conditions, appropriate grade materials should be selected according to the specific environment.

title: Tungsten Prices Exhibit Two Inverted V-Shaped Patterns in the First Half of 2026
text: Analysis of Latest Tungsten Market from Chinatungsten Online In the first half of 2026, building upon the cumulative price surge of over 220% seen in 2025, China's tungsten market experienced extreme volatility, characterized overall by two distinct "inverted-V" price cycles. Structural support from tight raw material supplies intertwined with the periodic release of downstream demand, driving tungsten prices to rapidly spike to historic peaks—surpassing expectations—before undergoing a deep correction and settling into a phase of fluctuating consolidation. First Major Volatility Cycle: Rapid Doubling Followed by Deep Correction At the start of the first half of the year, the market maintained the strong momentum seen at the end of 2025; tungsten prices accelerated upward due to persistent raw material supply tightness and expectations regarding the metal's strategic value. From early 2026 through mid-March—a span of just two and a half months—prices for major tungsten products doubled, building upon an already high baseline. The price of tungsten concentrate broke the RMB 1 million/ton mark, Ammonium Paratungstate (APT) climbed to a high of RMB 1.5 million/ton, and tungsten powder reached RMB 2.4 million/ton. This rally was driven primarily by supply-side constraints and market optimism regarding tungsten's strategic importance. However, pressure to lock in profits at these high price levels and the limits of downstream cost tolerance quickly became apparent. Starting in mid-March, the market trend reversed, shifting from a seller's market to a buyer's market. Over the subsequent two-plus months, the gains accumulated earlier in 2026 were entirely erased. This correction was steep and accompanied by a marked decline in trading activity, reflecting the supply chain's limited capacity to absorb such high price levels. Second Cycle: Weak Fluctuation After a Brief Rebound From late May through June, the tungsten market saw a modest rebound, supported by eased capital pressure upstream and the release of downstream demand for restocking at lower price points. However, due to a lack of sustained demand momentum, the rebound was limited and short-lived; the market subsequently entered a phase of weak fluctuation characterized by sluggish trading and slow inventory destocking. By the end of June, the price of 65% wolframite concentrate had fallen below RMB 500,000/ton, APT prices stagnated around RMB 700,000/ton, and tungsten powder prices fluctuated within the RMB 1.15 million/ton range. Based on trends observed in the first half of the year, the tungsten market has shifted from the one-way bull market of 2025 into a period of fluctuation; key variables remain the increase in supply-side resources, the pace of demand-side consumption, and shifts in market sentiment. According to research by China Tungsten Online, the prevailing industry expectation for prices is RMB 400,000-500,000/ton for tungsten concentrate and RMB 600,000-700,000 /ton for ammonium paratungstate (APT). However, given the significant market volatility over the past two years and the instability of the current international environment, considerable uncertainty regarding future market performance remains. Stakeholders are advised to closely monitor market data from China Tungsten Online, conduct rational analysis, and avoid making decisions based on emotion. title: The Production Method of Lanthanum Tungsten Electrodes
text: The production method of lanthanum tungsten electrodes is powder metallurgy technology, and its steps include doping process and coated powder preparation, press forming, high-temperature sintering, plastic working, and surface treatment, among others. 1.Doping process and coated powder preparation Doping is a key step affecting the uniformity of distribution of rare earth lanthanum oxide in the tungsten matrix. In industry, the solid-liquid doping method is mainly adopted, that is, mixing a lanthanum-containing compound solution with tungsten oxide or tungsten powder to obtain a precursor powder with uniform composition. The main doping methods include the nitrate method, acetate method, and mechanical mixing method. The nitrate method mixes lanthanum nitrate solution with tungsten oxide powder, and through heating concentration, drying, calcination, and reduction treatment, lanthanum nitrate is decomposed into lanthanum oxide, which is uniformly coated on the surface of tungsten particles, but the mixing uniformity is relatively high and nitrogen oxide gases are easily generated. The acetate method uses lanthanum acetate with tungsten oxide or tungsten powder and water to make a slurry, and after uniform mixing and reduction treatment, the lanthanum salt can be decomposed more fully, which helps improve the electrical conductivity of the material in subsequent processes while reducing harmful gas emissions. The mechanical mixing method mixes lanthanum oxide powder with tungsten powder, and the operation is relatively simple, but the mixing uniformity is limited by powder particle size and mixing time, and lanthanum oxide particles are prone to moisture absorption, which may affect the quality of subsequent press forming. Lanthanum Tungsten Electrode Picture 2.Press forming The prepared lanthanum-tungsten mixed powder is subjected to press forming to obtain green compacts with certain shapes, dimensions, and strength. Common forming methods include mechanical pressing and cold isostatic pressing. Cold isostatic pressing puts the powder into an elastic mold and then places it in a high-pressure liquid, applying uniform pressure in all directions, to obtain green compacts with more uniform density, and the weight of a single green compact can be controlled according to subsequent processing requirements. 3.Sintering process Sintering is the process of heating the green compacts to a high temperature under a protective atmosphere, causing diffusion and densification between tungsten particles, to obtain sintered bars with certain density and strength. This process has an important influence on the density, grain size, and distribution state of rare earth oxides of the electrode. Common sintering methods include vertical sintering, medium-frequency induction sintering, and hydrogen-protected sintering. Vertical sintering uses the resistance heat generated by electric current passing through the green compacts for sintering, and the sintering temperature needs to be controlled to avoid sharp growth of tungsten grains and segregation of rare earth oxides. Medium-frequency induction sintering combined with cold isostatic pressing can obtain electrode materials with sintering density within a certain range. Hydrogen-protected sintering is carried out in a pure hydrogen atmosphere to prevent tungsten from oxidizing at high temperatures, and through gradient heating and holding treatments, the density of the finished product can approach the theoretical density of tungsten. Lanthanum Tungsten Electrode Picture 4.Plastic working and surface treatment The sintered bars need to undergo plastic working to obtain finished electrodes of the required diameter and length. Plastic working is mainly carried out through multiple passes such as swaging and drawing, so that the cross-section of the bar is gradually reduced to reach the required wire or rod dimensions. During this process, plastic working can make the rare earth oxide second phase more evenly distributed in the tungsten matrix and also refine the tungsten grains. Recrystallization annealing treatment is carried out at appropriate times to eliminate work hardening and restore the plasticity of the material, facilitating subsequent processing. After the finished wire is straightened and ground, electrolytic polishing can also be used to reduce the surface roughness to an appropriate level, to meet dimensional tolerances and surface quality requirements. The dimensional tolerances and surface quality of finished lanthanum tungsten electrodes generally need to comply with relevant standards.

title: The Surface Sampling Results from the Pioneer Tungsten Project Have Been Released
text: Highlights of the surface sampling results from the Pioneer Tungsten Project in Montana: 1. Analytical results for 30 rock chip samples from the Pioneer Tungsten Project in Montana,have returned strongly anomalous tungsten (W) values, with a third of the samples collected containing over 500ppm tungstate (WO3), with maximum values of 3,159ppm (0.32%) WO3 for a garnet skarn float sample from Red Mountain’s Greenstone claim area and 2,856ppm (0.29%) WO3 from a skarn outcrop within the Mammoth claims. 2. The best results returned comparable values to the grade of Almonty’s Gentung Tungsten deposit, which lies within 200m of Red Mountain’s Mammoth claims. 3. The results confirm the presence of garnet skarn hosted W mineralisation within Red Mountain’s Pioneer Tungsten Project - with further, systematic sampling to be completed to better define the extent, variability and continuity of the mineralisation, prior to a decision on drill testing of one or more targets. 4.The Pioneer Tungsten Project comprises three claim areas – Greenstone, Mammoth and Lost Creek – located along the eastern margin of the Mount Torrey Batholith, which locally features massive limestone-hosted garnet skarns, up to 25m thick. These skarns are known to contain Tungsten mineralisation as scheelite (CaWO4). 5. Red Mountain’s Pioneer Tungsten Project claims encompass similar geology and lie adjacent to claims purchased in November 2025 by Almonty Industries (Market Cap AU$6.7 billion), hosting the Gentung Tungsten Deposit, with a mineral resource of 6.83Mt @ 0.315% WO3; as well as the Ivanhoe and Lost Creek Mines, which are estimated to have collectively produced 680kt of Tungsten ore in the 1950s and 1970s. 6. Further systematic sampling at the highest priority Greenstone prospect is planned for mid-July, with the Company expecting to be able to move rapidly to drill testing of downdip extensions of skarn mineralisation, subject to positive analytical results. 7. Drilling at the Armidale Antimony-Gold Project in NSW will commence this month with the drilling contractor secured. Red Mountain Mining Limited, a Critical Minerals exploration and development company with an established portfolio in Tier-1 Mining Districts in the United States and Australia, is pleased to announce that it has received analytical results for 30 due diligence rock-chip samples collected from the Mammoth and Greenstone prospects – two of the three areas that comprise the Company’s 100% owned Pioneer Tungsten Project in Montana, USA. Ten of the 30 samples (refer to Appendix 1) were found to contain over 500ppm tungstate (WO3), with five samples from the Greenstone area assaying at over 1,000ppm (0.10%) WO3, with a maximum value of 3,159ppm (0.32%) WO3; and one sample from the Mammoth prospect returning a result of 2,856ppm (0.29%) WO3. Six of the samples from the Greenstone area, including three samples containing >500ppm WO3, lie north of Red Mountain’s current claim footprint, within an area that the Company has staked and expects to be granted by the end of July 2026. Greenstone mine location and surface sample analysis results map（Source: Red Mountain） Further sampling to define potential drill targets The assay results confirm the presence of garnet skarn hosted Tungsten mineralisation at surface within Red Mountain’s Pioneer Tungsten Project, with the best results returning comparable values to the grade of Almonty’s Gentung tungsten deposit, which lies within 200m of Red Mountain’s Mammoth claims and has an estimated mineral resource of 6.83Mt @ 0.315% WO33. Further systematic sampling will be completed by Red Mountain to better define the extent, variability and continuity of the surface mineralisation. This work will initially focus on the highest priority Greenstone prospect, with sampling planned for mid-July, following which the Company expects to be able to move rapidly to drill testing of downdip extensions of skarn mineralisation, subject to positive analytical results. Mammoth mine location and surface sample analysis results map（Source: Red Mountain） Pioneer Project Geology The Pioneer Tungsten Project claims cover three discrete locations, the Greenstone, Mammoth and Lost Creek prospects, where the eastern margin of the Uphill Creek Granodiorite is in direct contact at surface with the Snowcrest Range Group. Red Mountain’s claims encompass Tungsten- bearing skarn mineralisation mapped and sampled in the middle of last century and a number of historical workings still visible today. The claims also lie immediately adjacent to claims purchased in November 2025 by Almonty Industries, which include the Gentung Tungsten Deposit, which has a total mineral resource of 6.83 Mt @ 0.315 % WO3; as well as the Ivanhoe and Lost Creek Mines, which are estimated to have collectively produced 680kt of tungsten ore in the 1950s and from 1970 to 1975. Pioneer tungsten project surface geological map（Source: Red Mountain） In addition to the exposures of garnet skarn at surface, Red Mountain’s claims also have clear geological potential for limestone-hosted tungsten-bearing garnet skarn mineralisation at shallow depths beneath overlying quartzite units, where magnetic modelling undertaken by Arrow Geosciences, indicates subsurface magnetic bodies, interpreted to represent the granodiorite source of the skarn mineralisation. The Torrey Batholith is a large volume composite complex that forms the core of the Pioneer Mountains in southwest Montana. The batholith ranges in composition from gabbro to granite, but is dominantly granodioritic in composition. Tungsten mineralisation occurs along the entire eastern contact of the Pioneer Batholith where it is in contact with mid-Paleozoic carbonate-rich sedimentary rocks, but to date significant mineralisation, occurring in scheelite-bearing massive garnet skarns, has only been found where the limestones of the Snowcrest Range Group contact the Uphill Creek Granodiorite. Significantly, there does not appear to be any skarn development or tungsten mineralisation associated with the Grayling Lake Granite, which cuts and is therefore younger than the granodiorite and associated skarn mineralisation at the Mammoth Prospect. Tungsten mine pictures Historical tungsten production The earliest recorded interest in the garnet skarn hosted tungsten mineralisation surrounding the Mount Torrey Batholith dates from the early 1950s, driven by the US Federal Government’s strategic metal stockpiling program, with significant production recorded from the Ivanhoe and Lost Creek mines. Exploration for tungsten was carried out between 1951 and 1953 around the Ivanhoe Mine (also known as the Brown’s Lake Mine), which had been mined for copper, silver and gold in 1928 and 1929, recording production of 5.7t Cu; 647 oz Ag and 1 oz Au. Open pit tungsten production from the Ivanhoe Mine commenced in October 1953 and initially ceased in 1957, with total production during this period of 567kt at an average grade of 0.35% WO3. Similar skarn-hosted tungsten mineralisation was mined by the Minerals Engineering Company between 1952 and 1956 from a series of adits and small open pits at the Lost Creek Mine, ~5km southeast of Ivanhoe. The total recorded production from Lost Creek during this period is 19kt at an average grade of 0.18% WO3. Both mines remained idle until 1971, when General Electric purchased the properties and rebuilt the mill at Ivanhoe, which operated until 1975. Minor Tungsten production is also recorded from the Greenstone Mine during the 1950s, with recorded production of 900kg of sorted ore, containing 1.2% WO3. It is estimated that total production from the district from the 1950s and 1970s is approximately 680kt of tungsten ore。 Source: Red Mountain

title: Chinese Traders Actively Snap Up US Tungsten Scrap
text: According to the *Financial Times*, Chinese traders have been aggressively sourcing tungsten scrap across the United States since early 2025. This activity has sparked fierce bidding wars with domestic recyclers, pushing tungsten prices significantly higher. The report notes that Chinese buyers are contacting long-standing US suppliers directly, often offering prices far above those of domestic recyclers—sometimes as much as five times the standard market rate. Consequently, the price of US tungsten scrap has surged by 350% since May 2025, while the price of tungsten metal has risen by more than 200%. This trend unfolds against the backdrop of a global tungsten supply shortage. China has long dominated the global tungsten industry, accounting for over 50% of global mining and refining output while also consuming roughly half of the world's tungsten supply. However, in recent years, China has restricted production through domestic mining quotas and, in early 2025, implemented export restrictions on various critical minerals, including tungsten. Furthermore, declining production capacity at aging Chinese mines has further driven the country to seek new sources of supply overseas. Tungsten is a vital strategic metal widely used in sectors such as aerospace and defense—for applications ranging from armor-piercing munitions and missiles to industrial tool manufacturing. As geopolitical tensions intensify, nations are placing greater strategic importance on critical mineral resources, viewing them as core elements of national security and industrial development. Although China bans the import of tungsten scrap for environmental reasons, it can import processed tungsten products that meet regulatory standards. Reports indicate an increase in US scrap exports to recycling hubs in the Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam, and South Korea, though the ultimate destination of these materials remains unconfirmed. The United States has reacted strongly to this situation. The US has had no commercially operating tungsten mines since 2015 and relies on large annual imports of processed tungsten. Currently, US tungsten stockpiles are low, and domestic processing capacity is insufficient. Government authorities have pledged to revitalize the domestic mining industry and ensure supply chain security, with plans to invest in tungsten mining projects in countries like Kazakhstan to diversify supply sources.

title: Tungsten Wire Tendon Ropes for Bionic Robotic Arms
text: Bionic robotic arms typically employ a tendon-driven mechanism that mimics human tendons; fine ropes or cables actuate the joints to enable flexible, multi-degree-of-freedom movement. This design allows heavy components (such as motors) to be positioned at the arm's base or forearm, thereby reducing weight at the extremity and enhancing flexibility, responsiveness, and biomimetic fidelity. The use of tungsten wire tendon ropes in bionic robotic arms represents a cutting-edge technological trend. Why use tungsten wire tendon ropes for bionic robotic arm transmission? 1. High Strength and Load-Bearing Capacity: Tungsten’s tensile strength (approx. 980 MPa) far exceeds that of stainless steel (approx. 621 MPa). This allows for thinner ropes capable of withstanding greater tensile forces, meeting the requirements for high-degree-of-freedom movement and strong gripping force in dexterous robotic hands. 2. Fatigue Resistance and Long Service Life: Tungsten wire tendon ropes from CTIA GROUP excel in environments involving repeated bending and flexing, with a fatigue life exceeding one million cycles—significantly outperforming stainless steel wire ropes and certain polymer fibers. They are resistant to wire breakage, creep, and aging, ensuring the robotic arm operates stably over the long term during high-frequency tasks. 3. Adaptability to Harsh Environments: Leveraging the inherent properties of tungsten-based materials—such as resistance to high temperatures, corrosion, oxidation, and radiation—CTIA GROUP’s tungsten wire tendon ropes are reliably used in extreme operational scenarios, including medical surgical robots, aerospace, and the nuclear industry. They ensure system safety and continuity under rigorous conditions. 4. Low Friction and Precision Transmission: These ropes feature low internal friction and a low sliding friction coefficient. The transmission process is precise with minimal elastic recoil, enabling accurate and stable force and displacement transfer—making them ideal for bionic robotic arm tasks requiring high-precision operation. 5. Enhanced Composite Processing: While tungsten wire is inherently somewhat brittle, the use of advanced cold-drawing, stranding, and multi-strand composite techniques—or blending with other fibrous materials—significantly improves its flexibility. This results in a tendon that combines structural rigidity with bending flexibility, achieving an ideal balance of properties. Furthermore, in practical engineering applications, CTIA GROUP tungsten wire tendons can undergo surface treatments to further reduce wear and improve compatibility with joint pulleys, thereby extending the maintenance intervals for the entire actuation system. These combined advantages make tungsten wire tendons a key material choice for advancing the performance and reliability of bionic robotic arms.

title: Application of Tungsten Wire Tendon Ropes in Dexterous Hands
text: In the fields of humanoid robotics and precision manipulation, the dexterous hand is a core component for achieving high degrees of freedom (DOF), human-like grasping, and fine motor control. Its design must balance high precision, compliance, and reliability. Tendon-driven actuation—a mainstream approach—mimics human tendon structures by flexibly transmitting torque from remote actuators to finger joints; this significantly reduces hand inertia and enhances dexterity. Tungsten wire tendon ropes, braided from tungsten wire, are emerging as a key enabling material for high-end dexterous hands. 1. Core Characteristics of Tungsten Wire Tendon Ropes Tungsten wire possesses exceptionally high tensile strength—several times that of ordinary steel wire—along with a high melting point, wear resistance, and low creep. When fabricated into fine tendon ropes, they allow for extremely small bending radii without wire fraying or unraveling, meeting the demands of multi-directional, repetitive bending within the confined joint spaces of dexterous hands. Compared to stainless steel wire ropes, tungsten wire tendon ropes offer lower friction coefficients and reduced internal stress. Compared to UHMWPE (Ultra-High Molecular Weight Polyethylene) fiber ropes, they demonstrate superior performance regarding high loads, long-term fatigue resistance, and dimensional stability. They are particularly well-suited for scenarios involving continuous 24-hour industrial operation or medical sterilization cycles, as they are less prone to fatigue-induced breakage or loss of precision. 2. Application Principles in Dexterous Hands Typical tendon-driven dexterous hands employ a hybrid "motor + lead screw + tendon rope" structure. The actuator is in the forearm or palm; a lead screw converts the motion, and multiple tungsten wire tendon ropes then actuate the finger joints. A single five-fingered dexterous hand typically requires 12 to 24 tendon ropes, each independently controlled, to achieve 22 to 25 degrees of freedom (DOF). This approaches the capabilities of the human hand, supporting adaptive grasping, precision manipulation, and high load-bearing capacity. 3. Advantages of Tungsten Wire Tendons in Dexterous Hands High Load Capacity and Spatial Adaptability: The high strength of tungsten wire enables a small-diameter design that fits into confined spaces and facilitates the integration of high-DOF (Degrees of Freedom) systems. It provides ample tensile force, making it suitable for industrial gripping and minimally invasive medical instruments. High Precision and Compliance: Low friction and low creep ensure accurate force and displacement transmission. When combined with tension sensors, it enables closed-loop force feedback that simulates human tactile sensation, allowing for complex actions such as delicate pinching and object flipping. Reliability and Longevity: Excellent fatigue resistance—along with durability against oil, dust, and repeated bending—makes it suitable for diverse applications ranging from 3C electronics assembly and semiconductor sorting to surgical robotics. In the medical field, tungsten wire tendons are widely used in systems like the da Vinci, supporting over a thousand surgical cycles.

title: Garzê Prefecture Cracks Down on Illegal Mining of Tungsten and Other Mineral Resources
text: According to the Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture Bureau of Natural Resources and Planning, the prefecture recently held a video conference to launch a special campaign targeting the illegal mining of resources such as rare earth, gold, tungsten, and sand and gravel. Officials from the prefecture's natural resources and planning, public security, and water conservancy departments, as well as relevant county and city officials, attended the meeting. The meeting focused on implementing the provincial action plan and decided to establish dedicated task forces at both the prefecture and county levels. Counties and cities are required to immediately form joint action groups that coordinate law enforcement and public security resources, implementing a closed-loop management system that covers the entire process—from clue screening and case investigation to rectification and control. The campaign will proceed in two stages: a concentrated screening and remediation phase from June to November (featuring comprehensive, sweeping inspections, joint law enforcement, and a reward system for reporting violations) and a review and summary phase in December. The Bureau of Natural Resources and Planning, the Public Security Bureau, and the Water Conservancy Bureau reported on initial results and outlined next steps. They called for the use of big data to strengthen the coordination between administrative enforcement and criminal justice. Focusing on minerals such as rare earth, gold, tungsten, and sand and gravel, authorities will conduct carpet-style inspections of active mining sites, old mine shafts, abandoned mining areas, closed mines, sand and gravel processing plants, and agricultural/breeding sites. The campaign aims to crack down on illegal activities while reinforcing rectification and source-level controls to ensure effective remediation and safeguard the prefecture's mineral resources and ecological security. Situated at the headwaters of the Yangtze and Yellow Rivers and atop the highlands of western Sichuan, Garzê Prefecture boasts a vast territory, holds significant ecological importance, and is rich in natural resources. According to the “Garzê Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture Mineral Resources Master Plan (2021–2025)”, the prefecture is a key part of the renowned "Three Rivers" metallogenic belt in Southwest my country. Its mineral resources—characterized by rare metals, non-ferrous metals, precious metals, and geothermal energy—hold strategic importance within the province, and the mining industry possesses immense development potential. By the end of 2020, 74 types of minerals had been discovered, and 1,207 solid mineral deposits had been identified. Proven reserves include more than 40 mineral varieties—such as lithium, silver, lead, zinc, copper, gold, platinum, nickel, tin, tungsten, marble, geothermal resources, and mineral water—comprising 17 large-scale and 84 medium-scale deposits.

title: Applications of Tungsten Wire Tendon Ropes in Medical Rehabilitation Robots
text: As a high-performance transmission component, the tungsten wire tendon rope is manufactured from fine tungsten filaments using a precision stranding process. It features exceptionally high tensile strength, excellent fatigue resistance, and a minimal diameter. In medical rehabilitation robotics, it serves as a superior alternative to traditional stainless steel wire ropes and polymer fiber ropes, acting as a key material for achieving precise, compliant, and safe actuation. Its application not only enhances the performance of rehabilitation equipment but also provides patients with more reliable movement assistance and support for functional recovery. 1. Material Properties and Advantages of Tungsten Wire Tendon Ropes The core competitive advantage of tungsten wire tendon ropes stems from the unique physicochemical properties of tungsten. With a melting point as high as 3422°C and strong resistance to oxidation and corrosion, the material withstands repeated high-temperature, high-pressure sterilization (above 121°C) and ethylene oxide disinfection cycles; it retains over 95% of its strength without significant creep or aging. This is crucial for medical environments, where traditional polymer fiber ropes often suffer performance degradation after sterilization, and stainless steel wire ropes pose risks of wire breakage and biocompatibility issues. Tungsten wire tendon ropes comply with ISO 10993 biocompatibility standards; they feature a low coefficient of friction and excellent flexibility, allowing them to wrap around micro-pulleys with diameters as small as 2mm and enabling high-degree-of-freedom bending without compromising transmission precision. Furthermore, the fatigue life of tungsten wire tendon cables far exceeds that of traditional materials, maintaining stability through thousands to tens of thousands of tensile-relaxation cycles. This ensures reliable long-term, continuous operation for medical rehabilitation robots, making them particularly suitable for repetitive training scenarios involving patients with stroke, spinal cord injuries, or post-operative orthopedic conditions. 2. Specific Applications of Tungsten Wire Tendon Ropes in Rehabilitation Robots In hand rehabilitation robots, tungsten wire tendon ropes (such as those from CTIA GROUP) are frequently used in tendon-driven dexterous hands or exoskeleton structures. Remote motors pull the tendon ropes to actuate finger joints, enabling precise movements such as flexion, extension, and grasping. Compared to rigid linkage mechanisms, tendon-driven systems are lightweight and highly compliant; they better mimic human tendon biomechanics, thereby reducing the risk of secondary injury to the patient's skin and joints. Their minimally invasive design allows the device to conform to the limb and accommodate patients of various body types, enabling personalized force-feedback control that aids in the recovery of fine motor functions. Lower-limb rehabilitation robots—such as gait-training exoskeletons—also benefit from this technology. Tungsten wire tendons from CTIA GROUP can be integrated into flexible actuation modules for the hip, knee, and ankle joints, enabling coordinated, multi-degree-of-freedom movement. Distributed sensors and closed-loop control systems allow for real-time adjustment of tension magnitude and timing, assisting patients with movements like walking and squatting while reducing the robot's overall inertia and enhancing wearer comfort. In continuum robots—such as those for wrist or spinal rehabilitation—tungsten wire tendons drive the bending of flexible arms to conform to complex human body contours and provide smooth trajectory tracking, making them suitable for hybrid passive-active training modes in neurological rehabilitation. In scenarios combining surgery and rehabilitation, tungsten wire tendons also support robots designed for early post-operative mobility assistance, ensuring precise control of the device within confined spaces or complex postures and helping to shorten recovery times. Driven by an aging population and rising demand for rehabilitation, the medical rehabilitation robotics market is expanding rapidly. Thanks to their reliability, safety, and precision, tungsten wire tendons are poised to become a key enabling technology, playing an increasingly important role in portable home rehabilitation devices, remote teleoperation systems, and multimodal training platforms.

In practical applications, this characteristic helps form relatively uniform welds, reduce weld bead deflection or molten pool fluctuation caused by arc instability, thereby improving the overall weld density and surface quality. This characteristic is of great significance in aerospace welding, where human health and environmental protection requirements are relatively high. Compared with early thorium-containing tungsten electrodes, lanthanum tungsten electrodes are more convenient in meeting relevant safety standards, can reduce potential risks, and have become a common alternative choice in the aerospace field. CTIA GROUP's lanthanum tungsten electrodes are suitable for both DC and AC welding tasks and have good compatibility with argon shielding gas commonly used in aerospace welding. title: Which Has Stronger Arc Starting Capability Between Lanthanum Tungsten Electrodes and Cerium Tungsten Electrodes?
text: Lanthanum tungsten electrodes and cerium tungsten electrodes produced by CTIA GROUP are both types of rare earth tungsten electrodes, and both have certain application value in industrial welding and plasma processing fields. However, according to differences in electron work function and oxide content, there are corresponding differences in arc starting performance between the two. CTIA GROUP's lanthanum tungsten electrodes picture The electron work function range of CTIA GROUP's lanthanum tungsten electrodes is generally 2.6–3.2 eV, with typical specifications including WL10 type (2.8-3.2 eV), WL15 type (2.8-3.0 eV), and WL20 type (2.8-3.2 eV). The electron work function of cerium tungsten electrodes is generally around 2.7–2.8 eV. This value enables cerium tungsten electrodes to require relatively lower voltage when striking an arc under low-current conditions, and the electron emission process facilitates arc starting at lower open-circuit voltages. In practical applications, the doping of cerium oxide can improve arc starting characteristics, especially showing certain advantages in DC welding tasks. In low-current DC welding applications, the arc starting performance of cerium tungsten electrodes is relatively outstanding, and they can ignite the arc more easily under lower voltage conditions. This benefits from their relatively low electron work function and characteristics under DC positive polarity conditions. In contrast, the arc starting capability of lanthanum tungsten electrodes has certain advantages in the medium-current range, and the presence of lanthanum oxide helps maintain arc continuity while reducing flickering during repeated ignition occasions. CTIA GROUP's lanthanum tungsten electrodes picture The lanthanum oxide doping in CTIA GROUP's lanthanum tungsten electrodes can effectively inhibit grain growth, enhance the thermal stability of the electrode, and make the arc relatively stable during maintenance. Cerium tungsten electrodes exhibit good arc column control characteristics under low-current conditions, avoiding frequent instability. The uniform oxide distribution in both electrode types helps maintain tip shape under arc action and reduce arc starting difficulties caused by thermal shock. According to oxide content, the current-carrying capacity of lanthanum tungsten electrodes is improved compared with pure tungsten electrodes, and they are suitable for medium to relatively high current ranges. Cerium tungsten electrodes have higher arc starting sensitivity in low-current applications, allowing arc starting and maintenance at lower current densities.

This value makes the arc starting process relatively easy, especially showing stable performance under AC welding or high-current conditions. In practical applications, the WL20 type can reduce downtime during arc maintenance and repeated ignition occasions, while also lowering the electrode burning rate. title: How Should Cerium Tungsten Electrodes Be Stored?
text: The cerium tungsten electrodes produced by CTIA GROUP, as an electrode type with cerium oxide (CeO₂, content about 1.8% to 2.2%) added to the tungsten matrix, are prone to react with oxygen in the air on their surface to form an oxide layer, which can change their electron work function, reduce arc starting sensitivity, and shorten service life. Therefore, taking appropriate storage measures can effectively maintain electrode surface cleanliness and functional stability, which helps maintain relatively high arc performance and consistency in precision welding scenarios. CTIA GROUP and its parent company, CHINATUNGSTEN ONLINE, have been dedicated to the tungsten-molybdenum products industry for nearly 30 years. They specialize in providing flexible, customized global services for tungsten-molybdenum products, designing, manufacturing, and precisely processing various standard specifications, grades, and dimensional precision according to customer requirements, suitable for a wide range of applications. For more information on tungsten electrodes, please visit the website: http://www.tungsten.com.cn/tungsten-electrodes.html. If you require tungsten electrodes, please contact CTIA GROUP: sales@chinatungsten.com, 0592-5129595. CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes picture I. Causes of Surface Oxidation Phenomena of Cerium Tungsten Electrodes The tungsten matrix of CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes is itself relatively active. Although the cerium oxide additive can provide a low work function surface layer, slow oxidation reactions still occur with oxygen in room temperature or low-temperature storage environments. The oxidation reaction mainly forms a dense oxide layer on the electrode surface, which affects electron emission capability, especially making arc starting difficulties or arc jitter more likely to occur during low-current or AC welding. Studies show that the formation of an oxide layer reduces the electrical conductivity of the electrode tip, increasing burn-off rate and reducing overall stability. II. Storage Environment and Conditions for Cerium Tungsten Electrodes To prevent surface oxidation of cerium tungsten electrodes, it is recommended to store them in a well-ventilated, dry environment with relative humidity below 60%. The storage area should avoid contact with moisture, grease, or other contaminants. Electrodes should be stored in sealed original packaging containers, or vacuum packaging can be used to further isolate them from air. This storage method can effectively reduce oxygen contact opportunities, keeping the electrode surface clean and its function unchanged. Studies show that storing in a low-temperature dry environment significantly reduces the surface oxidation rate of electrodes, which has practical value in applications with strong production continuity. CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes picture III. Specific Operation Points for Storing Cerium Tungsten Electrodes When storing CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes, the electrode tips should be kept dry, avoiding wiping with water or other liquids. Packaging integrity should be regularly checked, and damaged packaging should be replaced promptly. In the workshop, cerium tungsten electrodes can be stored separately from other metal materials to avoid surface contamination from oil or foreign matter. In actual production, when used in conjunction with high-frequency arc starting devices, care should also be taken during storage to avoid contact between the electrode tips and hard objects, as mechanical damage may accelerate oxidation. These measures help maintain the effective distribution of cerium oxide, ensuring that the electrodes can still perform good arc starting and stable arc states after long-term storage. IV. Influence of Storage Conditions on Cerium Tungsten Electrode Performance Cerium tungsten electrodes stored in dry environments have a slow oxide layer formation on the surface, and electron emission capability remains in good condition. In AC aluminum welding or thin plate low-current welding, these electrodes can maintain stable arc starting and relatively low burn-off rate. Studies show that electrodes stored under appropriate conditions generally have a longer single-use service life and more consistent heat-affected zone control during use. This helps achieve reliable welding results in applications with high quality requirements such as medical devices or precision structural component welding.

title: Cerium Tungsten Electrodes for Thin Plate Low-Current Welding
text: During welding processes such as tungsten inert gas welding (TIG welding), thin plate low-current welding (generally referring to operations with plate thickness of 0.5mm to 1.5mm and current in the range of 5A to 30A) has certain specific requirements for electrode selection. The cerium tungsten electrodes produced by CTIA GROUP, as tungsten-based electrodes containing cerium oxide (CeO₂), show good adaptability in this scenario. Their outstanding low-current arc starting performance and good arc stability can effectively reduce electrode burn-off and heat input, which has practical value in applications requiring weld quality control. They specialize in providing flexible, customized global services for tungsten-molybdenum products, designing, manufacturing, and precisely processing various standard specifications, grades, and dimensional precision according to customer requirements, suitable for a wide range of applications. Process Characteristics of Thin Plate Low-Current Welding Thin plate low-current welding mainly involves seam treatment of materials such as stainless steel or titanium alloys. These materials tend to have relatively small heat-affected zones and low deformation risk under low-current conditions. Cerium tungsten electrodes (common specification WC20, with cerium oxide content of about 1.8% to 2.2%), due to their strong electron emission capability and high arc starting sensitivity, can maintain stable arc starting and combustion characteristics when used in low-current DC or AC mixed applications. Studies show that in welding of 0.5mm to 1.0mm thin plates, using 1.0mm diameter cerium tungsten electrodes with low-current settings can effectively reduce electrode tip temperature and burn-off rate. II. Electron Emission and Arc Starting Advantages of Cerium Tungsten Electrodes in Thin Plate Low-Current Welding Electron work function is a key factor affecting electrode arc starting performance. The electron work function of pure tungsten electrodes is about 4.5 eV, while the incorporation of cerium oxide can reduce it to the range of about 2.7 eV to 2.8 eV, significantly improving thermionic emission capability. In thin plate low-current scenarios, this characteristic of cerium tungsten electrodes manifests as relatively low arc starting voltage and high re-ignition frequency. Studies show that after doping with cerium oxide, the arc starting efficiency of the electrode under low current (5A to 20A) is significantly improved, reducing the risk of welding interruption caused by arc jitter or failure to ignite. CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes picture III. Current Carrying and Burn-Off Control of Cerium Tungsten Electrodes in Thin Plate Low-Current Welding CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes have relatively excellent current carrying capacity at low currents, supporting about 20% to 40% additional capacity compared to pure tungsten, while maintaining a relatively low burn-off rate. Industry practice shows that in welding of 0.5mm thin plate stainless steel, when cerium tungsten electrodes (diameter 1.0mm) are operated in the current range of 5A to 15A, the single-use electrode service life is generally longer, with burn-off mainly concentrated at the electrode tip rather than the overall matrix. Under the action of the arc, cerium oxide particles migrate to the tip, forming a low work function surface layer, reducing high-temperature wear and evaporation loss. This helps maintain a stable electrode state during long-term low-current operations, extend single-use duration, and reduce downtime caused by frequent electrode replacement.

title: Comparison Between Cerium Tungsten Electrodes and Thorium Tungsten Electrodes
text: During the tungsten inert gas welding (TIG welding) process, the cerium tungsten electrodes and thorium tungsten electrodes produced by CTIA GROUP, as common electrode types with added rare earth oxides, have certain differences in arc starting, combustion stability, and overall usage characteristics. These differences mainly affect the welder's choice of electrode, depending on the welding current range, base metal type, and process requirements. CTIA GROUP and its parent company, CHINATUNGSTEN ONLINE, have been dedicated to the tungsten-molybdenum products industry for nearly 30 years. They specialize in providing flexible, customized global services for tungsten-molybdenum products, designing, manufacturing, and precisely processing various standard specifications, grades, and dimensional precision according to customer requirements, suitable for a wide range of applications. For more information on tungsten electrodes, please visit the website: http://www.tungsten.com.cn/tungsten-electrodes.html. If you require tungsten electrodes, please contact CTIA GROUP: sales@chinatungsten.com, 0592-5129595. CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes picture I. Composition of Cerium Tungsten Electrodes and Thorium Tungsten Electrodes Cerium tungsten electrodes (commonly WC20 specification) are typically made by adding about 1.8% to 2.2% cerium oxide (CeO₂) to a tungsten matrix, with no radioactive components. Their tip color corresponds to gray, and their electrical conductivity and arc characteristics are manifested as easy arc starting at relatively low currents and good re-ignition capability. Thorium tungsten electrodes (commonly WT20 specification) are made by adding about 1.7% to 2.2% thorium oxide (ThO₂) to a tungsten matrix, with the tip color usually being red. They have strong electron emission capability and can provide relatively high arc stability in DC welding. II. Comparison of Electron Emission Capability Between Cerium Tungsten Electrodes and Thorium Tungsten Electrodes Electron emission capability is a key factor in electrode arc starting. The electron work function of pure tungsten electrodes is about 4.5 eV, and this value can be significantly reduced by adding rare earth oxides. Cerium tungsten electrodes, through the addition of cerium oxide, can reduce the electron work function to the range of about 2.7 eV to 2.8 eV, exhibiting excellent low-current arc starting and re-ignition characteristics, especially suitable for thin plate or precision welding applications. In comparison, thorium tungsten electrodes, through the addition of thorium oxide, can also reduce the electron work function (to about 2.6 eV), providing good arc starting performance, but their advantage is more pronounced in DC applications. III. Comparison of Current Carrying Capacity Between Cerium Tungsten Electrodes and Thorium Tungsten Electrodes Cerium tungsten electrodes generally have relatively high current carrying capacity at lower current settings, with an increase of about 20% to 40% in capacity compared to pure tungsten electrodes, making them suitable for medium to low current precision operations. Thorium tungsten electrodes have stronger carrying capacity at higher currents, supporting a larger current range, while the operating temperature is generally below the melting point, providing a relatively long single-use service life. According to actual process experience, in DC welding of metals such as stainless steel, thorium tungsten electrodes have a lower burn-off rate and uniform wear, helping to extend service life. Cerium tungsten shows lower evaporation loss during low-current continuous operation, but it should be noted that at high currents, oxides may migrate to the tip, affecting long-term stability. Common data indicates that under the same electrode diameter, thorium tungsten typically has a service life about 10% to 20% longer than cerium tungsten at medium currents, which is practical in high-frequency production applications. Comparison of Arc Stability and Weld Quality Between Cerium Tungsten Electrodes and Thorium Tungsten Electrodes Both CTIA GROUP’s cerium tungsten electrodes and thorium tungsten electrodes can provide relatively stable arc states, but cerium tungsten has smaller arc jitter amplitude and uniform burn-off characteristics at low currents, making it suitable for applications requiring fine control of weld formation. Thorium tungsten exhibits higher arc stability in DC high-current welding, reducing arc wandering. In terms of weld quality, the amount of tungsten transferred from thorium tungsten electrodes to the weld pool is generally lower, reducing the risk of weld contamination. Cerium tungsten, due to the distribution characteristics of its cerium oxide, can form a more uniform arc in AC welding, reducing the risk of defects such as porosity or undercut. Selection of Lanthanum Tungsten Electrodes for Medical Device Welding The diameter of CTIA GROUP’s lanthanum tungsten electrodes is generally matched to the base metal thickness, with 1.0mm to 3.2mm being the common range. However, with the improvement of environmental protection and safety requirements, rare earth tungsten electrodes have gradually become their alternative. Rare earth tungsten electrodes are non-consumable electrode materials made by adding a certain proportion of rare earth oxides to a tungsten matrix, including cerium tungsten electrodes (cerium oxide content about 1.8%~2.2%, gray tip), lanthanum tungsten electrodes (lanthanum oxide content about 1%~2%, sky blue or gold tip), and yttrium tungsten electrodes. In addition, thorium tungsten electrodes have a relatively high crystallization temperature, superior electrical conductivity, and good mechanical cutting performance. These characteristics make the electrode less prone to deformation under high-temperature arc action, with strong oxidation resistance. The core advantage of rare earth tungsten electrodes lies in the fact that the addition of oxides effectively reduces the electron work function, thereby improving electron emission capability. Compared with thorium tungsten electrodes, cerium tungsten electrodes also have a relatively low electron work function (generally in the range of 2.7eV to 2.8eV) and usually have relatively high current carrying capacity at low current settings. Cerium tungsten electrodes have good crystallization temperature and electrical conductivity, low melting rate and long service life, especially with excellent arc starting performance in low-current DC welding. Lanthanum tungsten electrodes also have a relatively low electron work function, showing good arc stability and strong re-ignition capability in DC welding, with a long service life in the medium current range. Yttrium tungsten electrodes have the best arc concentration under high-current conditions, suitable for thick plate processing, and their ablation resistance is outstanding in automated welding. CTIA GROUP’s thorium tungsten electrode picture Thorium tungsten electrodes are mainly suitable for DC welding and cutting processes, widely covering materials such as carbon steel, stainless steel, nickel alloys, and titanium alloys. When using DC positive polarity connection, they can provide stable arc, good penetration control, and relatively high current carrying capacity. Among rare earth tungsten electrodes, cerium tungsten electrodes are more suitable for low-current or thin plate welding, suitable for connection of pipes, pipe products, and small precision components. In AC argon arc welding or plasma cutting, their burn-off is relatively large, and the allowable welding current range is generally smaller than that of thorium tungsten electrodes. Lanthanum tungsten electrodes perform well in both DC and AC mixed use, with current carrying capacity close to the electrical conductivity of 2% thorium tungsten electrodes, and have good ablation resistance at medium currents. Yttrium tungsten electrodes show stronger penetration control under high-current conditions, suitable for occasions with high stability requirements such as aerospace.

Compared with traditional cutting methods, plasma cutting has the characteristics of fast cutting speed, narrow kerf, small deformation, and wide applicability to materials, especially outstanding in thick plate cutting of stainless steel, aluminum alloys, titanium alloys, and carbon steel. Arc drift is prone to occur during long-term welding, and stability in low-current precision welding is average. WT20: Industry common balanced model, with sensitive arc starting, concentrated arc convergence, small drift, smooth arc re-ignition during AC/DC switching, and is the optimal choice for most welding conditions. WT40: The work function is relatively low, and the arc can be started at ultra-low voltage. The arc rigidity is relatively strong in high-current, intermittent welding, and plasma welding, with almost no arc drift; however, excessive ThO₂ is prone to agglomeration, and spot-like ablation pits may appear at the tip. 2.Current Carrying Capacity, High-Temperature Resistance, and Burn-out Life of Thorium Tungsten Electrodes Thorium particles are uniformly dispersed at tungsten grain boundaries, dissipating heat and delaying tip melting. The upper limit of current carrying capacity increases with thorium content. Current carrying capacity comparison (same diameter, DCEN): (1) WT10: Increased by about 12% compared to pure tungsten, suitable for small to medium current (50~150A) thin plate welding. (2) WT20: Increased by about 20% compared to pure tungsten, with relatively low loss in the 100~300A range, and the tip maintains a conical shape for a long time during continuous welding, not prone to rounding or sagging. (3) WT40: The upper limit of current carrying capacity is relatively high, dedicated to thick plates above 300A, plasma arc welding, and electron beam cathodes. Under the same current, the burn-out rate is 15%~25% lower than that of WT20. ThO₂ inhibits high-temperature coarsening of tungsten grains. The higher the thorium content, the higher the recrystallization temperature of the thorium tungsten electrode, making it less prone to coarsening and sagging under long-term high temperatures; WT40 is suitable for continuous high-current long-duration operations. Low thorium content: Tungsten at the tip evaporates faster, and tungsten particles are prone to falling off, causing tungsten inclusions in the weld. High thorium content: Tungsten matrix evaporation is inhibited by the ThO₂ film, resulting in higher weld cleanliness, but WT40 may precipitate trace impurities of thorium oxide at excessively high temperatures. 3.Physical, Mechanical, and Processing Properties of Thorium Tungsten Electrodes The hardness and brittleness of thorium tungsten electrodes increase with the amount of thorium oxide added. (1) WT10: Best plasticity, easy to sharpen, not prone to edge chipping, less grinding dust, friendly to small-batch manual grinding. (2) WT20: Moderate hardness, suitable for industrial mass production grinding and cutting, balancing toughness and high-temperature strength. (3) WT40: Brittleness increases significantly, prone to tip chipping during grinding, prone to cracking during cutting, high processing loss, and reduced yield. CTIA GROUP’s thorium tungsten electrode picture 4.Radioactive Safety of Thorium Tungsten Electrodes ThO₂ releases alpha rays, with weak external penetration, and the risk is concentrated in the inhalation of grinding/cutting dust. (1) WT10: Lower total thorium content, weakest dust radioactivity, and lowest protection requirements. (2) WT20: Conventional industrial usage, moderate radiation, requiring wet grinding and ventilation in the workshop. (3) WT40: Thorium content is doubled, dust radiation intensity increases significantly, and long-term batch processing requires professional radiation protection workstations. 5.Electrical Conductivity, Thermal Conductivity, and Oxidation Resistance of Thorium Tungsten Electrodes Thorium oxide has lower thermal conductivity than metallic tungsten. The higher the thorium content, the slightly lower the thermal conductivity of the thorium tungsten electrode: WT10 has good thermal conductivity and fast heat dissipation, suitable for short-time pulsed low current; WT40 has stronger heat retention, maintaining emission temperature at the tip, suitable for continuous high-temperature cathode conditions; high-temperature oxidation resistance: WT40 > WT20 > WT10, forming a dense thorium-tungsten composite oxide film on the surface, reducing nitriding and oxidation ablation.
