title: Performance of Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouple Wire
text: Tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire is an alloy wire with tungsten (W) as the matrix and an appropriate amount of rhenium (Re) added. Commonly used types are WRe3/25 (Type D) and WRe5/26 (Type C). It possesses an extremely high melting point, excellent high-temperature thermoelectric properties, and good machinability, making it one of the mainstream metal thermocouple materials currently used for ultra-high temperature (especially above 1600℃) temperature measurement. It is widely used in vacuum furnaces, hydrogen atmospheres, inert gas environments, and high-end fields such as metallurgy, aerospace, and single-crystal silicon growth. The performance of tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire is described below. I. High-Temperature Performance Wide temperature range: Long-term operating temperature is typically 0–2300℃, and it can operate stably in vacuum, hydrogen, or inert atmospheres; short-term maximum temperature can reach approximately 3000℃. In industrial applications, due to limitations imposed by the protective tube and insulation materials, the common upper limit is mostly 1500–2000℃, with special structures allowing for even higher temperatures. High melting point: The melting point of alloys is generally above 3000℃ (pure tungsten is about 3410℃, high-rhenium alloys are slightly lower), far exceeding that of ordinary metal thermocouples. Low vapor pressure: Low volatilization loss at high temperatures, which is beneficial for long-term stable use. II. Thermoelectric performance Large thermoelectric potential and high sensitivity: The absolute value of the thermoelectric potential is about 2 to 3 times that of platinum-rhodium thermocouples. The Seebeck coefficient is high in the medium and high temperature range (approximately 16 to 22 μV/℃), resulting in sensitive response and a strong output signal. Good temperature-thermoelectric potential relationship: Good linearity over a wide temperature range, facilitating calibration and use. Permissible deviation: ±4.0℃ in the 0–400℃ temperature range; ±0.25%t in the 400–2300℃ temperature range for WRe3/25 and ±0.5%t for WRe5/26 (t is the measured temperature); high-precision products can achieve even better levels. Non-uniform thermoelectric potential: The uniformity of the positive or negative electrode of the entire roll (reel) at 1200℃ generally does not exceed 40-80 μV. Good uniformity is beneficial to improving temperature measurement accuracy. III. Physical and Mechanical Properties Density: WRe3 approximately 19.16 g/cm³, WRe5 approximately 19.20 g/cm³, WRe25 approximately 19.58 g/cm³, WRe26 approximately 19.60 g/cm³. Room temperature resistivity: Increases with increasing rhenium content (WRe3 approximately 0.093 μΩ·cm, WRe26 on the order of 0.30 μΩ·cm). Excellent mechanical properties: The addition of rhenium results in a rhenium effect, significantly lowering the ductile-brittle transition temperature, improving room temperature and high-temperature plasticity, ductility, and processability, while maintaining high hardness and high strength. Annealed tungsten exhibits high tensile strength (≥1700MPa for some high-performance wires) and significantly better elongation than pure tungsten, facilitating drawing, winding, and assembly. High recrystallization temperature: beneficial for maintaining strength and structural stability at high temperatures. Resistance to thermal shock and fatigue: superior to pure tungsten, suitable for alternating thermal stress environments. IV. Chemical Stability and Operating Atmosphere Good stability in non-oxidizing atmospheres: excellent chemical stability in vacuum, dry hydrogen, and inert gases (such as argon and helium), allowing for long-term reliable operation. Extremely prone to oxidation: rapidly oxidizes and undergoes grain growth at high temperatures in air or oxygen-containing atmospheres, leading to embrittlement and performance degradation. It cannot be used exposed in oxidizing environments. It requires a ceramic protective tube, molybdenum/tungsten protective tube, or special anti-oxidation coating (such as multi-layer barriers) for use in certain oxidizing atmospheres. Sensitive to carbon atmospheres: easily forms carbides, leading to decreased sensitivity and brittle fracture. Carbonization is accelerated in the presence of hydrogen; careful atmosphere control is necessary during use. V. Other Comprehensive Advantages and Precautions Significant Cost Advantage: Price is significantly lower than platinum-rhodium thermocouples (approximately one-fifth to one-tenth of their price), offering high cost-effectiveness and making it suitable as a replacement for precious metal thermocouples in high-temperature applications. Fast Response and High Reliability: Fine wire diameter (commonly 0.08–0.5 mm) and small heat capacity result in rapid thermal response when in direct contact with the measured object; good mechanical strength and long service life (under suitable atmospheres). Usage Precautions: The uniformity of the microstructure directly affects service life and accuracy; the thermocouple becomes brittle after high-temperature use, so repeated bending should be avoided; the material and seal of the protective tube have a significant impact on actual performance. title: wrapable tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire

It is mainly used to manufacture ultra-high temperature thermocouples and is a typical representative of refractory metal thermocouple wires. 1. Definition and Composition of Wrapable Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouple Wire Tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire is composed of paired tungsten-rhenium alloy wires with different rhenium contents. The material has a high melting point of 3120-3360℃ and possesses high mechanical strength, stable electrical properties, and low vapor pressure. The addition of rhenium (Re) significantly lowers the ductile-brittle transition temperature, increases room temperature plasticity and recrystallization temperature, allowing the wire to pass bending tests and achieve the "wrapable" characteristic, facilitating subsequent processing into thermocouples or cathode wires. Common tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire models are WRe3/25 (positive electrode approximately 97% W - 3% Re, negative electrode approximately 75% W - 25% Re, corresponding to type D index) and WRe5/26 (positive electrode approximately 95% W - 5% Re, negative electrode approximately 74% W - 26% Re, corresponding to type C index). The wire diameter is typically 0.08-0.5 mm (tolerance ±0.02 mm). CTIA GROUP can customize finer or thicker specifications according to customer needs and actual application scenarios. 2. Performance Characteristics of Wound Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouple Wire Ultra-high Temperature Application Range: Long-term operating temperature in vacuum, hydrogen, or inert atmospheres can reach 0–2300℃, with short-term maximums approaching 2800–3000℃; data dispersion increases above 2300℃. Thermoelectric properties: High thermoelectric potential, high sensitivity, and good linearity of temperature-potential relationship; the non-uniform thermoelectric potential of the entire roll of wire at 1200℃ is generally controlled within 40–80 μV. Therefore, it must be used in a non-oxidizing environment or in conjunction with a dense protective tube. Cost and substitution advantages: The price is much lower than platinum-rhodium thermocouples, and it can partially replace precious metal thermocouples for ultra-high temperature measurement. 3. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Zirconia-Sheathed Thermocouples
text: In fields such as high-temperature single-crystal growth, aerospace thermal protection testing, and specialty metallurgical smelting, precise temperature measurement—often exceeding 1600°C or even 2000°C—is critical to the success of the process. Traditional platinum-rhodium (noble metal) thermocouples are unsuitable for such extreme temperatures, as they are prone to grain growth, softening, and even breakage (melting) above 1700°C. Tungsten-rhenium (W-Re) wire from CTIA GROUP serves as a high-performance temperature-sensing material; thanks to its ultra-high melting point and excellent thermoelectric properties, it is the premier choice for temperature measurement in the 1600°C–2300°C range. When used in highly oxidizing or corrosive environments, pairing the wire with a zirconia (ZrO₂) protection tube—which offers exceptional refractoriness and chemical stability—provides a robust shield for the internal W-Re wire. 1. Application Advantages of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire Tungsten-rhenium wire is currently the thermocouple material with the highest temperature resistance used in industrial applications; common combinations include W-3%Re/W-25%Re and W-5%Re/W-26%Re. While pure tungsten has a melting point as high as 3410°C, it becomes extremely brittle and hard after high-temperature recrystallization, making it difficult to process and use. The addition of rhenium (Re) triggers the "rhenium effect," which not only preserves tungsten's ultra-high melting point but also significantly lowers the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature, ensuring good toughness and tensile strength at high temperatures. CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire operates stably over long periods at temperatures between 1600°C and 2300°C, with a short-term measurement limit reaching up to 3000°C, effectively filling the performance gap left by noble metal thermocouples in the ultra-high temperature range. In addition to its superior heat-resistant physical properties, CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire also demonstrates significant advantages in terms of electrical characteristics for temperature measurement. Within the same high-temperature range, the thermoelectric electromotive force (EMF) output of tungsten-rhenium thermocouples is approximately two to three times that of platinum-rhodium thermocouples, demonstrating exceptionally high high-temperature sensitivity (thermoelectric power). This high sensitivity enables control systems to detect minute temperature fluctuations, thereby facilitating finer temperature feedback and regulation. Furthermore, the relationship between the tungsten-rhenium wire's thermoelectric EMF and temperature is highly linear across a broad high-temperature range; this simplifies calibration and signal conversion, significantly enhancing temperature measurement accuracy in ultra-high-temperature industrial control systems. 2. Synergistic Protection of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire by Zirconia Protection Tubes Despite their superior performance, tungsten-rhenium wires are highly susceptible to rapid oxidation and volatilization in oxidizing atmospheres at temperatures exceeding 400°C; consequently, they must be utilized in vacuum, purified inert gas (such as argon or helium), or reducing atmospheres. However, actual industrial environments often contain oxygen or corrosive media. In such cases, the use of a zirconia (ZrO₂—typically partially or fully stabilized zirconia) protection tube is critical. Zirconia protection tubes possess a melting point exceeding 2700°C, along with excellent high-temperature insulation, slag resistance, and strong oxidation resistance. By sealing the tungsten-rhenium wire within a zirconia tube—either under vacuum or filled with high-purity inert gas—the system leverages zirconia's ability to withstand external high-temperature oxidation while shielding the internal wire from contamination and oxidation, achieving a perfect synergy between high-temperature sensing capabilities and environmental adaptability. 3. High-Temperature Applications of Zirconia-Tube Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouples Thermocouples utilizing CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium wire as the sensing core and a zirconia tube as the protective barrier are widely employed in the most demanding high-temperature industrial and scientific research applications. (1) In high-temperature vacuum and induction melting furnaces, it serves as a core component for real-time temperature monitoring of molten steel, superalloys, and refractory metal melts; (2) during the sintering of specialized ceramics and ultra-hard materials (such as boron carbide and silicon nitride), it ensures the precise execution of sintering profiles; (3) in crystal growth furnaces (such as those for sapphire and monocrystalline silicon), the high sensitivity of tungsten-rhenium wire enables fine control of the thermal field, thereby improving crystal quality; (4) furthermore, in thermal testing of aerospace engine combustion chambers and rocket nozzles, zirconia-sheathed tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are among the very few reliable tools capable of direct, contact-based temperature measurement within the harsh, ultra-high-temperature environments. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Bendable Thermocouples
text: I. What is a bendable thermocouple? A bendable thermocouple is a highly flexible temperature sensor designed to adapt to complex installation spaces. By utilizing fine-diameter thermoelement wires, soft insulation layers, or armored structures, it can bend to a certain degree, facilitating installation in narrow, curved, or vibration-prone environments while maintaining measurement accuracy and response speed. Unlike traditional rigid thermocouples, which are structurally limited and difficult to install, the bendable design significantly enhances versatility—offering distinct advantages in high-temperature, vacuum, or specialized atmospheric conditions. II. What is tungsten-rhenium wire? Tungsten-rhenium wire is the core material used to manufacture bendable high-temperature thermocouples. It is produced by adding a specific amount of rhenium (Re)—commonly 3%, 5%, 25%, or 26%—to a tungsten (W) base to form an alloy wire. Typical pairings include WRe3/25 (Type D) and WRe5/26 (Type C). While pure tungsten has an extremely high melting point, it is brittle at room temperature and prone to brittle fracture after high-temperature recrystallization. The addition of rhenium creates the "rhenium effect," significantly improving ductility, resistance to recrystallization, and high-temperature strength. This makes the wire easier to draw into fine diameters (commonly 0.1–0.5 mm; CTIA GROUP can provide even finer or custom-diameter wires) and imparts excellent bendability. Tungsten-rhenium wire from CTIA GROUP has a melting point of approximately 3120–3360°C. It is suitable for long-term use at temperatures up to about 2300°C (and higher for short durations) in vacuum, dry hydrogen, or inert atmospheres. It offers high thermoelectric potential, high sensitivity, and good linearity. Furthermore, it is far more cost-effective than platinum-rhodium thermocouples; given my country's abundant tungsten resources, it delivers exceptional value for money. However, tungsten-rhenium wire is prone to oxidation and—in carbon-containing atmospheres—to carburization and brittle fracture. Therefore, it should not be directly exposed to air or oxidizing atmospheres; instead, it requires the use of dense protective sheaths (e.g., molybdenum, tantalum, or ceramic) or armored structures, along with atmosphere control. III. Applications of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Bendable Thermocouples Bendable tungsten-rhenium thermocouples leverage the high ductility and high-temperature performance of tungsten-rhenium wire, combining fine-gauge wire with flexible insulation or mineral-insulated metal sheathing. They feature small bending radii, flexible installation, rapid response, and excellent mechanical strength and vibration resistance, making them particularly suitable for space-constrained environments or applications requiring repeated bending and adjustment. Key application scenarios for CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire used in bendable thermocouples: Metallurgy: Rapid temperature measurement of molten steel and iron, and monitoring of vacuum or controlled-atmosphere melting furnaces. The fine-diameter, bendable structure facilitates insertion into melts or complex furnace interiors; the wire offers rapid response and lower costs compared to platinum-rhodium thermocouples. High-temperature vacuum and atmosphere furnaces: Vacuum heat treatment furnaces, single-crystal growth furnaces, sintering furnaces, etc. They provide long-term monitoring across the 0–2300°C range, with protective sheaths and armored structures ensuring gas-tightness and durability. Aerospace: Temperature monitoring of aero-engine exhaust plumes, rocket engine nozzles, and hot-section components of hypersonic vehicles. The bendable design allows for easy conformity to complex curved surfaces or tight spaces. Nuclear energy and scientific research: High-temperature measurement in nuclear reactors, materials research, and ultra-high-temperature experimental apparatus. They offer stability and reliability in vacuum or inert atmospheres, serving as a partial substitute for precious-metal thermocouples. Others: Electronic material preparation, sintering of special ceramics or refractory materials, and high-temperature chemical processes requiring ultra-high temperatures and flexible installation. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Plug-Type Thermocouples
text: CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire for plug-type thermocouples is a material specifically designed for ultra-high-temperature measurement. Produced by alloying tungsten with an appropriate amount of rhenium, these wires form a stable thermoelectric potential when used in pairs. They are utilized in quick-connect plug-type thermocouple assemblies to ensure reliable temperature detection in high-temperature environments. 1. Basic Composition of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Plug-Type Thermocouples Tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wires consist of matched pairs of alloys with varying rhenium content. Common combinations include WRe3/25 (Tungsten-3% Rhenium positive leg paired with Tungsten-25% Rhenium negative leg, corresponding to Type D) and WRe5/26 (Tungsten-5% Rhenium positive leg paired with Tungsten-26% Rhenium negative leg, corresponding to Type C). These wires typically range from 0.1 mm to 0.5 mm in diameter and feature high melting points and good ductility. In plug-type thermocouples, the ends of the wires connect to standardized plugs or compensating plugs, facilitating quick insertion/removal and instrument interfacing, thereby enhancing on-site usability. 2. Temperature Measurement Principle of Plug-Type Thermocouples The temperature measurement principle of plug-type thermocouples is based on the Seebeck effect: a circuit is formed by joining the ends of two tungsten-rhenium alloy wires of different compositions. When a temperature difference exists between the measuring junction and the reference junction, a thermoelectric potential is generated in the circuit. This potential corresponds to the temperature, allowing the measured temperature to be determined through instrumentation. 3. Characteristics of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Plug-Type Thermocouples CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire exhibits outstanding adaptability to high-temperature environments. It has a melting point of 3120–3360°C and can operate for extended periods between 0°C and 2300°C—and even at higher temperatures for short durations—in vacuum, dry hydrogen, or inert atmospheres. Compared to platinum-rhodium thermocouples, it offers a higher thermoelectric output and greater sensitivity, exhibits better linearity in its temperature-EMF relationship, and has significantly lower raw material costs, making it a viable alternative to noble metal thermocouples in certain applications. The material also maintains good mechanical strength and stable electrical properties at high temperatures. However, it is highly susceptible to oxidation failure in oxidizing atmospheres; therefore, practical application requires the use of a sealed protective tube (such as corundum, molybdenum, or a composite tube) to exclude oxygen and ensure a controlled internal atmosphere. 4. Application scenarios for plug-type thermocouples using tungsten-rhenium wire CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire is primarily used in applications requiring contact-based, ultra-high-temperature measurement, such as vacuum furnace temperature monitoring, rapid molten steel temperature measurement, aero-engine exhaust plume detection, high-temperature environments in the nuclear industry, and various aerospace and materials high-temperature tests. The plug-type configuration is particularly well-suited for scenarios requiring frequent replacement or rapid installation, such as expendable temperature measurement in metallurgical operations or flexible laboratory setups. Compared to traditional noble metal thermocouples, tungsten-rhenium wire offers a higher upper temperature limit and superior cost-effectiveness in the ultra-high-temperature range. Compared to other high-temperature sensors, it provides faster response times, allows for direct contact with the measured medium, and achieves high measurement accuracy when properly configured. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Tungsten Tube Thermocouples
text: The tungsten tube tungsten-rhenium thermocouple is a high-temperature measurement assembly featuring tungsten-rhenium wire as the high-precision temperature-sensing element and a tungsten tube as the protective sheath. It is widely used for temperature measurement in ultra-high-temperature environments across industries such as metallurgy, aerospace, nuclear energy, and chemical processing. I. Advantages of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire The tungsten-rhenium wire produced by CTIA GROUP is an alloy composed of tungsten and rhenium. When used as the temperature-sensing element in a thermocouple, it offers the following outstanding advantages: 1. Ultra-high melting point and wide temperature measurement range CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium alloy has a melting point of 3120–3360°C, making it one of the most heat-resistant metallic thermocouple materials available. In non-oxidizing atmospheres, the standard operating temperature range is 0–2300°C, with short-term operating temperatures reaching 2800°C. 2. Excellent thermoelectric properties Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples feature a linear relationship between temperature and electromotive force (EMF) and offer reliable thermal stability. The alloy generates significant thermoelectric potential, resulting in thermocouples with high sensitivity and measurement accuracy. Furthermore, the magnitude of the thermoelectric potential depends solely on the alloy composition and the temperature difference between the two ends, remaining independent of the thermocouple's shape, length, or diameter. 3. Superior mechanical and chemical properties CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire exhibits high strength at both room and elevated temperatures, good ductility after recrystallization, high resistivity, and a low temperature coefficient of resistance. Chemically, it offers resistance to oxidation and carburization, strong resistance to water-cycle reactions, and excellent weldability. It maintains good chemical stability in non-oxidizing atmospheres. 4. Fast response speed and high cost-effectiveness Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples offer rapid response times; when in direct contact with the object being measured, they are unaffected by intermediate media and react sensitively to temperature changes. Additionally, they are relatively inexpensive, serving as a viable alternative to costly platinum-rhodium thermocouples in certain applications. II. Advantages of Tungsten Tubes Tungsten tubes from CTIA GROUP are primarily used as protective sheaths for thermocouples; their advantages include: 1. Excellent High-Temperature Performance Pure tungsten possesses an extremely high melting point and boiling point, as well as excellent high-temperature strength and creep resistance. In protective atmospheres—such as a vacuum, hydrogen, or inert gases—tungsten tubes can operate at temperatures up to 3100°C. Their upper operating temperature limit is 2300°C, far exceeding that of common protective tube materials like molybdenum (1900°C) and tantalum (1800°C). 2. Favorable Physical Properties CTIA GROUP tungsten tubes feature high thermal conductivity and a low coefficient of thermal expansion. At 1600°C, the coefficient of thermal expansion is 4.98 × 10⁻⁶. These tubes offer extremely high purity—typically exceeding 99.95%—and a density of over 18.2 g/cm³. 3. Outstanding High-Temperature Stability and Thermal Shock Resistance Tungsten tubes do not soften during prolonged operation at thermocouple working temperatures; they can function at the thermocouple's maximum temperature limit without degrading or deforming. Additionally, they exhibit good resistance to rapid temperature fluctuations and possess excellent overall thermal shock resistance. 4. Good Gas-Tightness and Corrosion Resistance CTIA GROUP tungsten tubes provide the gas-tightness, mechanical strength, and stability required for thermocouple protection. Tungsten metal resists various corrosive environments, including concentrated acidic and alkaline solutions. III. Applications of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire in Tungsten-Tube Thermocouples When paired with tungsten tube protective sheaths, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples enable precise temperature measurement in diverse high-temperature and harsh environments. Key application areas include: 1. Metallurgical Industry CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are widely used for temperature measurement in iron and steel smelting and high-temperature industrial furnaces. High-precision tungsten-rhenium thermocouples can replace S-type platinum-rhodium thermocouples within the 1000–1600°C temperature range. In environments with extremely harsh operating conditions, platinum-rhodium thermocouples have a service life of only about two weeks; in contrast, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples not only serve as a cost-effective alternative to expensive platinum-rhodium models but also offer a significantly longer service life. 2. Vacuum Furnaces and Heat Treatment CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are suitable for temperature measurement in high-temperature vacuum furnaces and various heat treatment furnaces, including vacuum furnaces for powder metallurgy and high-temperature sintering furnaces. When equipped with a tungsten protective tube, they enable reliable temperature measurement across the 0–2300°C range in vacuum, inert, and reducing atmospheres. 3. Aerospace and Nuclear Industries CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are widely used in the aerospace and nuclear energy sectors. Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples with a diameter of 0.255 mm have proven ideal for measuring temperatures in exhaust plume gas flows. They also serve as vital temperature measurement tools in ultra-high-temperature applications, such as nuclear reactors. 4. Chemical and Building Materials Industries Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are extensively used in industries such as petrochemicals (for high-temperature cracking furnaces and coking units), chemical kiln operations, and glass manufacturing. When fitted with specialized protective tubes, they can be used for extended periods in oxidizing atmospheres at temperatures up to 1600°C. 5. High-Temperature Thermocouple Calibration CTIA GROUP tungsten tubes are also utilized as furnace tubes for tungsten-rhenium thermocouple calibration furnaces. Vacuum tungsten tube furnaces can reach maximum operating temperatures of 2500°C, meeting the requirements for the graduation and calibration of tungsten-rhenium thermocouples.

title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Terminal-Head Thermocouples
text: A terminal-head thermocouple is a standardized industrial temperature sensor that utilizes a sealed terminal head at the top to facilitate and protect wire connections. Tungsten-rhenium wire enables the sensor to achieve high-temperature measurement capabilities exceeding 2000°C. These two components complement each other, making them indispensable in high-temperature industrial automation and control. I. Structure of Terminal-Head Thermocouples The front end of a terminal-head thermocouple consists of a temperature-sensing protection tube, while the rear features a terminal head made of metal or high-strength plastic, housing a terminal block. During operation, the thermocouple wires connect to compensation leads or signal transmission lines within the head, which serves to secure and protect the connections. This structure offers several significant advantages: (1) Robust environmental protection: The terminal head typically features waterproof, dustproof, and even explosion-proof capabilities, effectively shielding internal terminals from moisture, corrosive gases, and mechanical damage found in industrial environments. (2) Stable signal transmission: The terminal block provides reliable bolted connections, preventing poor contact or circuit breaks caused by external pulling forces or vibrations. (3) Convenient installation and replacement: The terminal head usually comes with standard threads or flange connections for easy mounting onto reaction vessels, furnace walls, or pipelines; maintenance does not require dismantling the entire sensor, as the wiring can be replaced simply by opening the head cover. II. Performance Characteristics of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire Tungsten-rhenium wire is a refractory alloy composed of tungsten (W) and rhenium (Re); it is currently the primary thermocouple wire material used in industry for measuring ultra-high temperatures ranging from 1300°C to 2300°C. Common pairings include WRe3-WRe25 and WRe5-WRe26, where the numbers indicate the percentage of rhenium added. Tungsten-rhenium wire from CTIA GROUP (Zhongtung Zhizao) possesses the following characteristics: (1) Ultra-high melting point and temperature resistance: With a melting point exceeding 3000°C, it can operate stably for extended periods at extreme temperatures above 2000°C. (2) Excellent thermoelectric performance: High thermoelectric power and sensitivity, with a signal output stronger than that of traditional noble metal thermocouples. (3) High cost-effectiveness: Within the 1300°C to 1800°C range, the overall cost is far lower than that of noble metal thermocouples (such as platinum-rhodium types). (4) Operating conditions: Rapid oxidation occurs in air at temperatures above 400°C; therefore, operation requires a protective atmosphere, such as a vacuum, a reducing gas (e.g., hydrogen), or an inert gas (e.g., argon). III. Applications of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Terminal-Head Thermocouples Combining the industrial-grade protective structure of a terminal head with the ultra-high-temperature measurement capabilities of tungsten-rhenium wire creates the terminal-head tungsten-rhenium thermocouple. Because tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wires are prone to oxidation, the sensing element is typically encapsulated within a sealed, airtight protective tube (made of materials such as corundum, molybdenum, or tantalum) that is either evacuated or filled with inert gas, while the terminal head is positioned in an ambient-temperature zone outside the furnace body. Key application scenarios for CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire (designed for terminal-head thermocouples) include: (1) Industrial vacuum furnaces and high-temperature sintering equipment: Installed on vacuum heat treatment furnaces, powder metallurgy sintering furnaces, and silicon carbide sintering equipment; the probe extends into the furnace's ultra-high-temperature zone, while the terminal head is fixed outside the furnace wall, enabling safe, automated temperature control. (2) Single-crystal and semiconductor material growth: Used in monocrystalline silicon pullers, sapphire growth furnaces, and chemical vapor deposition (CVD) reaction chambers; the protective tube extends into the high-purity, high-temperature reaction zone, and the terminal head transmits stable, high-precision temperature signals to the control system. (3) High-temperature metallurgy and waste gasification: Used for temperature monitoring at the roofs or walls of special alloy smelting furnaces, high-temperature slag pools, and high-temperature waste gasifiers, withstanding the dual challenges of internal high temperatures and harsh external industrial environments. (4) Scientific research and aerospace high-temperature testing: Used in large-scale laboratory setups—such as testing platforms for the fire resistance of high-temperature materials and simulated high-temperature nuclear reactor loops—providing ultra-high-temperature measurement interfaces that comply with industrial wiring standards. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Fixed-Assembly Thermocouples
text: In the field of modern industrial high-temperature measurement, the accurate and reliable acquisition of temperature data—ranging from 1,000°C to over 2,000°C—is crucial for ensuring product quality, equipment safety, and process optimization. As a mainstream component for contact-based temperature measurement, the performance of a thermocouple directly determines measurement accuracy and service life. Thanks to their extremely high melting points, excellent thermoelectric stability, and relatively cost-effective nature, CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wires have become the ideal alternative to precious-metal platinum-rhodium thermocouple wires for ultra-high-temperature environments. Meanwhile, the fixed-assembly structure ensures robust installation, excellent sealing, and ease of maintenance and replacement, enabling long-term, stable operation in demanding industrial settings. I. What is a fixed-assembly thermocouple? An assembled thermocouple is a temperature sensor that operates based on the thermoelectric effect (Seebeck effect). It consists of two conductors (thermocouple wires) of different compositions welded together at their ends to form a temperature-sensing circuit. When a temperature difference exists between the measuring junction and the reference junction, a thermoelectric electromotive force is generated in the circuit, allowing the corresponding temperature value to be read via a display instrument. As one of the most widely used temperature-sensing components in industry, assembled thermocouples are typically paired with display instruments, recorders, and electronic regulators to directly measure the temperature of liquids, vapors, gases, and solid surfaces. Structurally, an assembled thermocouple comprises a terminal box, a protection tube, insulating sleeves, terminal blocks, and thermoelements (thermocouple wires), along with various mounting fixtures. Depending on the mounting method, they can be categorized into types such as fixed-thread, fixed-flange, movable-flange, and welded-mount. Specifically, fixed-assembly thermocouples are securely mounted onto the equipment or pipeline being measured using threads, flanges, or welding; they are characterized by reliable installation, good sealing, and ease of maintenance and replacement. Materials for the protection tube—such as stainless steel, ceramics, or corundum—can be selected based on the operating environment to suit various temperature ranges and media conditions. Fixed-assembly thermocouples cover a measurement range of 0°C to 1800°C and are widely used in industrial sectors such as power generation, metallurgy, chemicals, and machinery manufacturing. II. What is Tungsten-Rhenium Wire? Tungsten-rhenium wire is a fine alloy wire made from a tungsten base doped with 1% to 30% rhenium (by mass fraction), along with trace amounts of silicon, aluminum, and potassium to enhance high-temperature performance. Tungsten-rhenium wire from CTIA GROUP possesses a range of excellent physicochemical properties: an extremely high melting point (up to 3300°C), low vapor pressure, high strength at both room and elevated temperatures, good ductility after recrystallization, high resistivity with a low temperature coefficient of resistance, as well as strong resistance to oxidation, carburization, and water-cycle reactions, along with excellent weldability. As a thermocouple material, tungsten-rhenium wire is one of the most important materials for high-temperature measurement. Depending on the tungsten-rhenium ratio, common types include WRe3/25 and WRe5/26; for instance, the positive leg of the WRe3/25 type consists of 97% tungsten and 3% rhenium, while the negative leg consists of 75% tungsten and 25% rhenium. Thermocouples made from CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium wire offer outstanding advantages, such as rapid response times, a wide temperature measurement range, and high thermoelectric electromotive force (EMF) and sensitivity. In vacuum, hydrogen, or inert atmospheres, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples can operate at temperatures of 2000–2400°C for long periods and up to 3000°C for short durations, making them one of the most reliable contact-type industrial thermocouples for measuring temperatures above 1800°C. However, since tungsten-rhenium wire oxidizes easily in oxidizing atmospheres, its use typically requires a protective sheath (such as a molybdenum alloy sheath) or other anti-oxidation measures. III. Applications of Fixed-Assembly Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouples Constructed using CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium wire as the thermoelement material and featuring a fixed-assembly structure, these thermocouples combine the ultra-high-temperature measurement capabilities of tungsten-rhenium materials with the installation reliability and ease of maintenance inherent in fixed-assembly designs. They offer a temperature measurement range of 0–1800°C (with some models exceeding 2000°C), high accuracy, stable performance, and cost-effectiveness, making them an ideal alternative to expensive platinum-rhodium thermocouples. Fixed-assembly tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are primarily used in the following sectors: Metallurgical Industry: Widely used in high-temperature applications such as metallurgical furnaces, powder metallurgy sintering furnaces, and molten steel temperature measurement. Under vacuum conditions, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples equipped with cermet protection tubes enable intermittent, in-line measurement of molten steel temperatures, meeting the requirements of vacuum metallurgy production processes. Chemical and Building Materials Industries: Used for temperature monitoring and control in high-temperature industrial furnaces, including coking furnaces, chemical kilns, glass melting furnaces, and cement kilns. They also play a vital role in chemical processing equipment involving specialized atmospheres, such as heavy oil cracking furnaces and coal gasifiers. Aerospace Sector: Employed in demanding, ultra-high-temperature scenarios such as measuring combustion gas temperatures in solid-propellant rocket engines, detecting aero-engine exhaust plumes, and conducting vacuum thermal testing for spacecraft. Research indicates that tungsten-rhenium thermocouples exhibit excellent resistance to high pressure and high temperatures during rocket engine ignition tests. Nuclear Energy Sector: Used in specialized environments such as nuclear reactor core temperature measurement. Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples can serve as a partial replacement for platinum-rhodium thermocouples for ultra-high-temperature measurement within nuclear reactors. Additionally, fixed-assembly tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are widely used in heat treatment furnaces, vacuum furnaces, and high-temperature electronic thermal systems. Thanks to their exceptionally high upper temperature limits, superior thermoelectric performance, and reliable installation structures, they have become indispensable sensors in the field of high-temperature industrial temperature measurement. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Simple-Structure Sheathed Thermocouples
text: CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire for simple-structure sheathed thermocouples is a specialized thermocouple wire material designed for high-temperature measurement. Composed of tungsten (W) and rhenium (Re) alloys, it is primarily used to manufacture simple-structure sheathed tungsten-rhenium thermocouples. This product combines the advantages of sheathed thermocouples—such as compact structure, flexibility, rapid response, and high-pressure resistance—with the ultra-high temperature measurement capabilities of tungsten-rhenium alloys, making it suitable for ultra-high-temperature applications in vacuum, reducing, or inert atmospheres. 1. Basic Composition and Common Models of Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouple Wire Tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire consists of a matched pair of wires made from tungsten-rhenium alloys with different compositions: the positive leg is typically a low-rhenium alloy (e.g., W-3%Re or W-5%Re), while the negative leg is typically a high-rhenium alloy (e.g., W-25%Re or W-26%Re). Common matched models include: WRe5/26 (Type C: W-5%Re vs. W-26%Re) and WRe3/25 (Type D: W-3%Re vs. W-25%Re). Wire diameters generally range from 0.08 mm to 1.0 mm (CTIA GROUP can design and customize specifications according to customer requirements), with a tolerance of approximately ±0.02 mm. Produced via processes such as powder metallurgy, vertical zone melting (sintering), swaging, and drawing, these wires feature a high melting point (approximately 3120–3360°C), relatively high ductility, and stable thermoelectric properties. In this simplified sheathed thermocouple, CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire serves as the temperature-sensing element (thermocouple leg). It is combined with high-purity insulation materials—such as magnesium oxide (MgO), aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃), or beryllium oxide (BeO)—and a protective sheath made of metals like molybdenum (Mo), tantalum (Ta), superalloys, or stainless steel. The assembly undergoes multiple stages of integral drawing to form a solid, non-detachable sheathed structure. The free end features a simple terminal box design, facilitating direct wiring or connection to compensation cables; this makes it ideal for applications where space is limited or cost-efficiency is a priority. 2. Performance Characteristics of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Simplified Sheathed Thermocouples Wide Temperature Measurement Range: Suitable for long-term use between 0°C and 2300°C, with short-term capability reaching 2800°C or higher (approaching 3000°C in a vacuum)—far exceeding the limits of standard base-metal or platinum-rhodium thermocouples. Thermoelectric Potential and Sensitivity: High thermoelectric potential rate (approximately 15–16 μV/°C), offering superior sensitivity compared to most noble-metal thermocouples and exhibiting good linearity. Mechanical and Physical Properties: Extremely high melting point and high strength; the addition of rhenium significantly improves the room-temperature brittleness of pure tungsten, ensuring the wire retains good ductility after recrystallization, which facilitates processing and the sheathing/drawing process. Sheathing Advantages: Can be manufactured with very small diameters (common outer diameters range from Φ2 mm to Φ20 mm, or even smaller); flexible, with a typical bending radius ≥5 times the outer diameter; features rapid thermal response, high mechanical strength, and resistance to vibration and high pressure. Accuracy Class: Typically categorized into Class I (approx. ±0.25%t) and Class II (approx. ±0.5%t). 3. Operating Conditions and Precautions for Tungsten-Rhenium Wire Direct use of tungsten-rhenium wire (and the sheathed thermocouples made from it) in oxidizing atmospheres is strictly prohibited, as rapid oxidation will lead to failure. Suitable environments include: vacuum, dry hydrogen, and inert gases such as argon or helium. When exposure to an oxidizing atmosphere is required, the thermocouple must be used in conjunction with a protective tube offering excellent gas-tightness (such as molybdenum, tantalum, or composite ceramic tubes). Direct contact with materials like quartz or graphite at high temperatures should be avoided to prevent contamination or failure. During the cooling phase after use, atmospheric protection must be maintained to prevent embrittlement of the thermocouple wires. 4. Application Areas for Simple-Type Sheathed Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouples These are primarily used for ultra-high temperature measurement, including: (1) temperature monitoring in vacuum furnaces and high-temperature heat treatment furnaces; (2) rapid temperature measurement of molten steel and other molten metals; (3) extreme high-temperature environments such as aerospace engine exhaust plumes and rocket nozzles; and (4) applications in the nuclear industry, semiconductor crystal growth furnaces, and high-power electronic devices. Compared to platinum-rhodium thermocouples, CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wires offer lower costs and a higher upper temperature limit, though they require stricter atmospheric controls; compared to standard K-type or N-type sheathed thermocouples, they significantly extend high-temperature application capabilities. The version featuring a simple terminal box is particularly well-suited for laboratories, testing equipment, or industrial measurement points with limited space, thanks to its streamlined structure and ease of installation. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Multi-Pair Sheathed Thermocouples
text: Tungsten-rhenium wire for multi-pair sheathed thermocouples is an ultra-high-temperature temperature-sensing material that integrates multiple sets of tungsten-rhenium alloy thermocouple wires into a single mineral-insulated sheathed structure. It features two or more pairs of tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wires arranged in parallel within a metal sheath, separated by high-purity insulating powder and formed into a unified assembly. This design enables simultaneous multi-point or redundant temperature measurement, combining ultra-high-temperature performance with a compact structure. 1. What is tungsten-rhenium wire? Tungsten-rhenium wire is an alloy wire made with a tungsten base and varying proportions of rhenium. Common pairings include WRe3/25 or WRe5/26, where the positive electrode contains a lower percentage of rhenium and the negative electrode contains a higher percentage to generate a stable thermoelectric potential. Produced by CTIA GROUP, these tungsten-rhenium wires feature high melting points and high thermoelectric output. They can operate in the 0–2300°C range within vacuum, dry hydrogen, or inert atmospheres, serving as core components for ultra-high-temperature contact temperature measurement. 2. What is a multi-pair sheathed thermocouple? A multi-pair sheathed thermocouple is a specialized type of thermocouple evolved from the traditional single-pair sheathed design. It embeds two or more pairs of thermocouple wires and high-purity insulating materials—such as magnesium oxide ceramic powder—into a single metal protective sheath. Through processes like integral drawing, these components are tightly bonded to form a permanent, integrated mineral-insulated sheathed structure. The wire pairs are strictly separated by insulation layers, allowing for independent signal output for multi-point measurement or mutual redundancy to enhance reliability, all while maintaining a relatively compact outer diameter suitable for installation in space-constrained environments. 3. Advantages of multi-pair sheathed tungsten-rhenium thermocouples Multi-pair sheathed thermocouples utilizing tungsten-rhenium wire retain the material's suitability for ultra-high temperatures and high sensitivity. Simultaneously, the sheathed structure provides excellent vibration resistance, pressure resistance, and flexibility. The multi-pair configuration allows for multi-channel measurement or redundant backup within a single sheath, thereby reducing the number of installation ports and wiring runs. Insulation and sheath materials must be compatible with the high-temperature and atmospheric conditions to ensure signal isolation and long-term stability. Compared to single-pair designs, this configuration offers distinct advantages in applications requiring high measurement point density or high reliability; however, strict avoidance of oxidizing atmospheres and proper sealing remain essential. 4. Applications of Multi-pair Sheathed Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouples Multi-pair sheathed tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are suitable for ultra-high-temperature environments requiring simultaneous monitoring of multiple adjacent points or system redundancy. Applications include multi-zone control in vacuum furnaces, parallel temperature measurement at critical points in high-temperature metallurgy, multi-point monitoring of aero-engine hot sections, and thermal protection testing in the nuclear and aerospace industries. They provide reliable contact-based temperature measurement in controlled atmospheres; their compact structure and rapid response help simplify system layout and enhance data integrity. In practice, the selection of sheath and insulation configurations, as well as cold-junction compensation and signal acquisition schemes, should be based on the number of measurement points, maximum operating temperature, and atmospheric conditions; additionally, it is recommended to contact CTOMS (China Tungsten) for compatible, high-performance tungsten-rhenium wire. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Sheathed Thermocouples
text: 1. What is a sheathed thermocouple? A sheathed thermocouple is a robust temperature sensor formed by tightly integrating thermocouple wires, high-purity insulating material (such as magnesium oxide ceramic powder), and a metal protective sheath through processes like integral drawing. The thermocouple wires are embedded within a high-density compressed insulation layer and encased in a metal sheath; both ends are sealed to create a permanent, integrated structure similar to mineral-insulated cable. This mineral-insulated, sheathed structure offers advantages such as flexibility, vibration resistance, high-pressure tolerance, rapid thermal response, high mechanical strength, and excellent airtightness. Its small outer diameter makes it suitable for applications with limited space or requirements for flexible installation. The measuring junction can be configured as insulated, grounded, or exposed to meet various temperature measurement needs. Sheathed thermocouples are widely used for temperature monitoring in industrial processes; they can measure medium temperatures directly or serve as the sensing element within assembled thermocouples. 2. What is tungsten-rhenium wire? Tungsten-rhenium wire is a high-performance thermocouple wire made from a tungsten base with the addition of an appropriate amount of rhenium. Common compositions include WRe3 (approx. 3% rhenium), WRe5 (approx. 5% rhenium), and high-rhenium alloys such as WRe25 and WRe26 (approx. 25%–26% rhenium). In thermocouple applications, low-rhenium alloy wires are typically paired with high-rhenium alloy wires to form combinations such as WRe3/25 (Type D) or WRe5/26 (Type C). The tungsten-rhenium wire produced by CTIA GROUP features a melting point as high as 3120–3360°C, a high thermoelectric potential rate, good high-temperature strength, and a degree of ductility. It operates stably within the 0–2300°C range in vacuum, dry hydrogen, or inert atmospheres, and can withstand temperatures approaching or exceeding 2800°C for short periods. It offers high sensitivity and relatively low cost, serving as a viable alternative to precious metal thermocouple wires (such as platinum-rhodium) for ultra-high-temperature contact temperature measurement. However, it is important to note that tungsten-rhenium wire oxidizes and fails rapidly in oxidizing atmospheres; therefore, strict atmospheric control or effective protective measures are essential during actual use. 3. Performance Characteristics of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Sheathed Thermocouples When tungsten-rhenium wire is incorporated into a sheathed structure, the resulting sheathed tungsten-rhenium thermocouple combines the ultra-high-temperature capabilities of the tungsten-rhenium material with the mechanical reliability of the sheathed design. Protected by the sheath and insulation layer, the thermocouple wires avoid direct exposure to the external environment, resulting in significantly improved vibration resistance, pressure resistance, and service life. The structure is flexible, offers a rapid thermal response, and features an adjustable outer diameter, making it suitable for complex installation conditions. In terms of performance, it retains the high melting point, high thermoelectric output, and wide temperature measurement range characteristic of tungsten-rhenium wire, capable of operating between 0°C and 2300°C in vacuum or inert atmospheres. Insulation materials must be selected to withstand high temperatures—such as beryllium oxide or hafnium oxide—while sheaths typically utilize refractory metals like molybdenum, tantalum, or tungsten alloys to ensure compatibility with the operating atmosphere and temperature. Compared to standard bare-wire or assembled tungsten-rhenium thermocouples, the sheathed configuration offers superior interference resistance and sealing performance; compared to sheathed precious metal thermocouples, it provides a higher upper temperature limit and lower costs. Operational precautions include avoiding oxidizing atmospheres and ensuring the long-term stability of the sheath and insulation materials. 4. Applications of Sheathed Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouples Sheathed tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are primarily used in applications requiring ultra-high temperatures, controlled atmospheres, and structural robustness. Typical scenarios include temperature monitoring in vacuum furnaces, temperature measurement during high-temperature metallurgical processes, testing of aero-engine exhaust plumes and hot-section components, high-temperature environments in the nuclear industry, as well as aerospace thermal protection testing and high-temperature material performance testing. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Single-Element Thermocouples
text: Tungsten-rhenium wire for single-element thermocouples refers to tungsten-rhenium alloy thermoelement wire specifically designed for use in single-element thermocouple structures. Made from tungsten-rhenium alloy, these wires are used in pairs to form the positive and negative electrodes of the thermocouple, thereby enabling the conversion and output of high-temperature signals. A single-element thermocouple is one that contains only one set (pair) of thermoelements internally; in other words, it has only one temperature-sensing junction and outputs a single temperature signal. Tungsten-rhenium wire is produced by melting and drawing tungsten and rhenium in specific proportions; it possesses an extremely high melting point, exceeding 3000°C. It also exhibits a favorable thermoelectric potential rate and sufficient ductility, allowing it to stably generate thermoelectromotive force (EMF) in ultra-high-temperature environments. 1. Working Principle of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire in Thermocouples When used as thermoelements, tungsten-rhenium wires operate based on the Seebeck effect. Two wires of tungsten-rhenium alloys with different compositions are joined at their ends to form a closed circuit; when a temperature difference exists between the measuring junction (hot junction) and the reference junction (cold junction), a thermoelectromotive force is generated within the circuit. The magnitude of this EMF is directly related to the temperature difference between the two junctions and the thermoelectric properties of the materials themselves. By measuring this EMF, the temperature being monitored can be calculated. The high thermoelectric potential rate and high-temperature stability of CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium alloys ensure reliable signal output even in the ultra-high-temperature range. In a single-element thermocouple, the tungsten-rhenium wires are encapsulated as a pair (one positive electrode and one negative electrode) within a protective tube or armored sheath. The ends are welded to form the measuring junction, while the cold ends are extended via wiring or connectors to complete the temperature-sensing circuit. This single-set structure outputs only one temperature signal; it is relatively simple in design, offers fast response times, and allows for cost-effective production. Common pairings for tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wires include WRe3-WRe25, WRe5-WRe26, and WRe5-WRe20. Generally, the positive electrode has a lower rhenium content (approximately 3% or 5%), while the negative electrode has a higher rhenium content (approximately 25% or 26%). 2. Key Applications of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire in Single Thermocouples Single thermocouples manufactured by CTIA GROUP using tungsten-rhenium wire are widely used in industrial applications requiring ultra-high-temperature measurement. In iron and steel smelting, they are frequently used for the rapid temperature measurement of molten metals, such as molten steel and iron. In equipment like vacuum furnaces and high-temperature sintering furnaces, they enable real-time monitoring of internal temperatures. They also leverage their high-temperature stability and sensitivity in applications such as powder metallurgy, cemented carbide production, and aero-engine exhaust plume monitoring. In certain specialized operating conditions, protective structures—such as molybdenum or corundum tubes—are employed to further extend service life. However, because tungsten-rhenium wire oxidizes very easily in air, atmospheric conditions must be strictly controlled during actual use; applications are typically limited to vacuum, hydrogen, or inert gas environments, or require the use of protective tubes. title: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Plug-in Thermocouples
text: Tungsten-rhenium wire for plug-in thermocouples refers to the tungsten-rhenium alloy wire used as the thermoelement in high-temperature thermocouples that utilize a plug-in (or push-pull/modular) connection structure. By combining the high-temperature measurement capabilities of tungsten-rhenium materials with the convenience of plug-in connections, this solution offers an important choice for industrial ultra-high-temperature measurement that balances performance with ease of use. 1. Working Principle of Plug-in Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouples The working principle of a thermocouple is based on the Seebeck effect: a circuit is formed by joining two conductors of different compositions at both ends; when a temperature difference exists between the two ends, a thermoelectric electromotive force (EMF) is generated, and the temperature can be determined by measuring this potential. Tungsten-rhenium wire is an alloy wire made from tungsten (W) and rhenium (Re) in specific proportions. Common pairings include WRe3/25 (positive electrode ~3% Re, negative electrode ~25% Re; corresponding to Type D) and WRe5/26 (positive electrode ~5% Re, negative electrode ~26% Re; corresponding to Type C). Tungsten-rhenium alloys from CTIA GROUP feature extremely high melting points (over 3000°C), good ductility, and high thermoelectric potential rates, making them suitable for ultra-high-temperature measurement. The "plug-in" designation indicates that the cold end (reference end) of the thermocouple utilizes a standard or specialized connector (plug/socket structure) rather than a traditional fixed terminal box. This facilitates the rapid connection and disconnection of compensation wires or instrumentation, making installation, replacement, and maintenance more convenient—a feature particularly useful in applications requiring frequent assembly and disassembly. 2. Characteristics of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Plug-in Thermocouples Temperature measurement range: Typically 0–2300°C (long-term use is usually around 2000°C, with higher temperatures possible for short-term use), far exceeding that of common K-type or S-type thermocouples. Operating atmosphere: Suitable for non-oxidizing environments such as vacuum, hydrogen, and inert gases. They oxidize and fail very easily in air or oxidizing atmospheres; therefore, they often require the use of protective tubes (such as those made of corundum, molybdenum, or tungsten) or an integrated oxidation-resistant design. Advantages: High thermoelectric potential and sensitivity; relatively abundant raw materials and lower costs compared to platinum-rhodium thermocouples, allowing them to serve as partial replacements for noble metal thermocouples. Limitations: Prone to recrystallization and embrittlement at high temperatures; strict atmospheric requirements; plug-in designs require attention to contact reliability and compensation matching. 3. Applications of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire for Plug-in Thermocouples Tungsten-rhenium wire for plug-in thermocouples produced by CTIA GROUP is widely used in high-end, high-temperature applications, including rapid temperature measurement of molten steel and metal melts, vacuum furnaces, high-temperature electronic thermal equipment, aero-engine exhaust plume monitoring, high-temperature monitoring in nuclear reactors, powder metallurgy, and cemented carbide production. title: Applications of Tungsten-Rhenium Thermocouple Wire
text: CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire is a refractory metal thermocouple wire made from a tungsten base alloyed with varying proportions of rhenium. Thanks to its exceptionally high maximum operating temperature, excellent thermoelectric properties, and superior mechanical characteristics, it plays an irreplaceable role in sectors such as aerospace, nuclear energy, metallurgy, petrochemicals, industrial process control, and scientific research. It serves as an effective, cost-efficient alternative to expensive platinum-rhodium thermocouples and represents a highly promising temperature-sensing material for high-temperature applications. The primary applications of tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire are outlined below. I. Aerospace Sector In the aerospace industry, CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire is primarily used to measure gas temperatures within solid-propellant rocket motors. The combustion environments in these motors involve high temperatures, high pressures, and rapid gas flow velocities, imposing extremely rigorous demands on temperature sensors. With advantages such as a maximum measurement temperature of 2800°C, high thermoelectric output, high sensitivity, excellent high-temperature performance, and cost-effectiveness, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are ideally suited to meet the specialized requirements of measuring internal combustion gas temperatures. Additionally, tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wire is used to measure combustion temperature distribution in rocket propellants. Compared to platinum-rhodium micro-thermocouples, tungsten-rhenium thermocouple wires offer ease of use, high spatial resolution, a high upper temperature limit, high thermoelectric output, and chemical inertness (lack of catalytic activity) regarding the surrounding atmosphere; these qualities make them ideal sensing elements for measuring temperature distribution across combustion waves. During missile ejection, fast-response tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are also employed to measure transient temperatures within the launch tube, enabling millisecond-level temperature monitoring in highly erosive environments. II. Nuclear Energy Sector In the nuclear energy sector, CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium thermocouples serve as instruments for ultra-high-temperature measurement within nuclear reactors. Specifically, they are used to monitor core temperatures in nuclear power reactors. To measure the centerline temperature of fuel pellets, high-temperature tungsten-rhenium thermocouple assemblies with metal sheaths have been developed; these utilize W-3%Re/W-25%Re core wires, BeO insulation, and molybdenum sheaths. Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples also serve as critical front-end sensors in nuclear research projects, such as experiments determining the equivalent thermal conductivity of pebble beds in high-temperature reactors. Additionally, thermocouples composed of tungsten, osmium-bearing alloys, and tungsten-rhenium alloys can operate effectively under nuclear irradiation conditions. III. Metallurgical Industry 3.1 Iron and Steel Smelting CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium rapid-response thermocouples are widely used for measuring the temperature of molten metals, particularly during steelmaking. In casting operations, these thermocouples can measure temperatures up to 2300°C; they offer a measurement success rate comparable to platinum-rhodium thermocouples and a temperature deviation of less than 10°C. 3.2 Powder Metallurgy and Non-ferrous Metallurgy Powder metallurgy products are typically manufactured in reducing atmospheres—such as hydrogen—which represents the ideal operating environment for tungsten-rhenium thermocouples. They also find extensive application in the field of non-ferrous metallurgy. 3.3 Heat Treatment and Coking In metallurgical heat treatment and coking processes, CTIA GROUP’s assembled high-temperature, high-pressure tungsten-rhenium thermocouples cover a temperature range of 0–1800°C. They offer advantages such as high precision, cost-effectiveness, stable performance, and immunity to atmospheric constraints. IV. Petrochemical Industry 4.1 Heavy Oil Cracking and Gasification Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are widely used to measure temperatures in petrochemical heavy oil cracking furnaces and coal gasifiers. In heavy oil gasifiers, they serve as a cost-effective alternative to expensive dual platinum-rhodium thermocouples for furnace temperature monitoring. They are particularly well-suited for high-temperature furnace gases containing over 95% CO and H₂, offering accurate measurement, rapid response to temperature fluctuations, and resistance to hydrogen embrittlement. Replacing Type B thermocouples with WRe3/25 thermocouples has yielded significant economic benefits. 4.2 Chemical Kilns and High-Temperature Cracking In high-temperature cracking furnaces within chemical plants, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples have been successfully used—paired with composite corundum protection tubes—to replace platinum-rhodium thermocouples in 1400°C reducing atmospheres. Additionally, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are widely utilized in industries such as coking and chemical kiln operations. 4.3 Special Material Production Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are also applied in the production of vanadium-nitrogen alloys, chromium-nitrogen alloys, boron carbide, and Si₃N₄ powders. V. Industrial Process Control and High-Temperature Measurement In the field of industrial process control, CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium thermocouples, when paired with display instruments, enable direct temperature measurement of liquid, steam, and gaseous media. They are suitable for use in environments characterized by strongly oxidizing or reducing atmospheres, vacuum conditions, high temperatures and pressures, and severe corrosion. Continuous temperature monitoring in carburizing furnaces and of high-temperature melts—such as molten aluminum and copper—represents another key application. Tungsten-rhenium thermocouples equipped with specialized protection tubes can operate for extended periods in oxidizing atmospheres at 1600°C. By applying oxidation-resistant coatings (such as a ZrB₂ and HfO₂ blend), these thermocouples can withstand oxidation for over 300 seconds in an oxidizing atmosphere at 2300°C. VI. Scientific Research and Temperature Measurement in Special Environments In scientific research, CTIA GROUP tungsten-rhenium thermocouples are widely used for temperature testing in explosion fields and for the dynamic diagnosis of transient temperatures under extreme operating conditions. In harsh environments like explosion testing sites, the combination of tungsten-rhenium temperature sensors, advanced power management modules, and dynamic data storage/testing technology ensures reliable temperature measurement. These thermocouples are also employed for ultra-high-temperature measurement (at 2100°C) in tungsten rod furnaces. title: The Cornerstone of Temperature Measurement in Reducing Atmospheres: Tungsten-Rhenium Wire
text: In high-temperature industrial sectors such as metallurgy, the nuclear industry, and aerospace, accurate temperature measurement within vacuum or reducing environments—such as those containing hydrogen—is critical. While traditional platinum-rhodium thermocouples are highly susceptible to corrosion and degradation in reducing media, tungsten-rhenium thermocouples have emerged as the premier solution for high-temperature measurement in these conditions, thanks to their exceptional thermal resistance and chemical stability. Tungsten-rhenium wire, serving as the thermocouple's thermoelement, is the pivotal material determining the accuracy and service life of the entire temperature measurement system. 1. Unique Material Advantages of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire in High-Temperature Reducing Environments Although tungsten possesses an extremely high melting point (approximately 3422°C), pure tungsten wire suffers from critical flaws: high brittleness at room temperature and a tendency to fracture easily following high-temperature recrystallization. By introducing rhenium as a solid-solution alloying element, CTIA GROUP produces tungsten-rhenium alloy wire that retains tungsten's high melting point while leveraging the "rhenium effect" to significantly enhance processing plasticity and high-temperature tensile strength. Crucially, when exposed to reducing atmospheres—such as hydrogen (H₂), carbon monoxide (CO), or high-purity inert gases—tungsten-rhenium wire does not undergo the volatile corrosion typical of oxidizing environments, thereby ensuring the physical structural integrity of the thermoelement material. 2. Thermoelectric Properties and Precision Control of Tungsten-Rhenium Wire As the sensing element of the thermocouple, CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wire is characterized by high thermoelectric electromotive force (EMF), high sensitivity, and excellent linearity between thermoelectric potential and temperature. Commonly used WRe3-WRe25 thermocouples deliver stable, reproducible millivolt signals across a broad temperature range of 0°C to 2300°C. To guarantee measurement precision, the manufacturing process demands rigorous control over alloy composition uniformity and impurity levels (such as oxygen, carbon, and iron). Even minute deviations in composition can lead to thermoelectric electromotive force (EMF) drift; therefore, high-quality thermocouple wires must undergo rigorous stress-relief annealing to ensure consistent thermoelectric properties along their entire length. 3. Key Application Scenarios for Tungsten-Rhenium Wire High-Temperature Vacuum and Hydrogen Furnaces: CTIA GROUP’s tungsten-rhenium wires are widely used in the temperature control systems of vacuum sintering furnaces, hydrogen reduction furnaces, single-crystal growth furnaces, and sapphire crystal growth furnaces, ensuring precise measurement during processes exceeding 2000°C. Aerospace and Defense Technology: Used in rocket engine nozzle testing, thermal protection system (TPS) trials for hypersonic vehicles, and temperature measurement of high-temperature reducing gas flows within ramjet combustion chambers. Nuclear Industry and Energy Sector: Plays an indispensable role in nuclear reactor core simulation tests, thermal performance evaluations of nuclear fuel rod cladding materials, and temperature measurement systems for high-temperature gas-cooled reactors. Semiconductor and Electronics Manufacturing: Used in Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) equipment and semiconductor epitaxial growth furnaces to monitor thin-film deposition temperatures within high-purity hydrogen atmospheres. 4. Precautions for Using Tungsten-Rhenium Wire Although tungsten-rhenium wire performs exceptionally well in reducing atmospheres, it is extremely sensitive to trace amounts of oxygen and moisture, undergoing rapid oxidation at temperatures above 400°C. Consequently, the sealing integrity and atmospheric purity of the measurement environment must be strictly maintained during use to prevent rapid degradation and failure of the wire due to minor oxidation. In practical engineering applications, tungsten-rhenium wires are typically paired with high-purity alumina (Al₂O₃) or beryllia (BeO) insulating tubes and encapsulated within protective sheaths made of materials such as molybdenum or tantalum.
